docs.title: FianchettoKit
docs.text:
Fianchetto's chess training logic as one Swift package: engine annotation, strength and Elo estimation, drill generation, spaced repetition, portable persistence, game import, and electronic-board handling — built on ChessCore.

FianchettoKit depends one-way on the ChessCore package (plus BoardKit for the board adapters) and targets iOS 18 / macOS 15, so it is free to use newer APIs and the networking stack.

The package holds decisions, not platforms. Its only imports are Foundation, ChessCore, and BoardKit with its board adapters — no SwiftUI, no UIKit, no SwiftData, no CloudKit anywhere in the sources. Storage, engine search, and model inference all sit behind protocols the platform shell implements, so the same code runs in the iOS/macOS app, in the Android (Skip/SkipFuse) port, and in a headless process.

docs.title: Running it headless
docs.text: fianchetto-cli exposes six of these seams as JSON-Lines filters — annotate, estimate, maia, accuracy, project, and track. It links the same FianchettoKit build the app ships, so a number it prints is the number the app would have computed for that input.

docs.title: A quick taste
docs.text:
import ChessCore
import FianchettoKit

// Record a tactics attempt against the Elo store (persisted via the seam).
var ratings = TacticsRatingStore.load(from: blobStore)
let delta = ratings.recordAttempt(
    puzzleKey: BlunderMasteryStore.key(fen: fen, correctSAN: "Qxh7"),
    difficulty: .medium,
    outcome: .correct,
    in: blobStore
)
print("rating \(delta >= 0 ? "+" : "")\(Int(delta))")   // "+12"

// Probe the Lichess tablebase for a 7-man endgame.
let result = try await TablebaseService.shared.probe(fen: endgameFEN)
print(result.category, result.bestMove ?? "—")

docs.title: Usage Examples
docs.text: Copy-paste recipes combining FianchettoKit with ChessCore. They assume a JSONBlobStore named blobStore (see Getting Started).

docs.title: A full tactics-attempt flow
docs.text:
Record one attempt against all three tactics stores and the mastery counter, with their shared key:

import ChessCore
import FianchettoKit

func recordTactic(
    position: Position,
    correctSAN: String,
    solvedCorrectly: Bool,
    elapsed: Double,
    difficulty: PuzzleDifficulty,
    in store: JSONBlobStore
) -> Double {
    let key = BlunderMasteryStore.key(fen: position.fen, correctSAN: correctSAN)
    let outcome: TacticsAttempt.Outcome = solvedCorrectly ? .correct : .wrong

    // 1. Elo.
    var ratings = TacticsRatingStore.load(from: store)
    let delta = ratings.recordAttempt(
        puzzleKey: key, difficulty: difficulty, outcome: outcome, in: store
    )

    // 2. Performance history.
    var perf = TacticsPerformanceStore.load(from: store)
    perf.record(
        TacticsAttempt(
            puzzleKey: key, outcome: outcome, elapsedSeconds: elapsed,
            attemptOrdinal: 1, extractionMode: "punish",
            difficulty: difficulty.rawValue
        ),
        in: store
    )

    // 3. Spaced-repetition mastery.
    BlunderMasteryStore.record(
        fen: position.fen, correctSAN: correctSAN,
        correct: solvedCorrectly, in: store
    )

    return delta   // for the "+12" / "−9" flash
}

docs.title: Show the due queue size for the Train hub
docs.text:
func updateTrainHub(
    masteryKeys: [(fen: String, san: String)],
    threshold: Int,                    // resolve with MasteryStreak.resolve(stored:)
    in store: JSONBlobStore
) {
    let due = masteryKeys.filter {
        !BlunderMasteryStore.isMastered(
            fen: $0.fen, correctSAN: $0.san, in: store, threshold: threshold
        )
    }.count
    let mastered = masteryKeys.count - due

    TrainProgressCache.record(
        .init(total: masteryKeys.count, due: due, mastered: mastered),
        for: .tactics,
        into: store
    )
}

docs.title: Probe a tablebase and pick the move that keeps the win
docs.text:
func tablebaseBestKeepingWin(for position: Position) async throws -> String? {
    guard TablebaseService.pieceCount(for: position) <= 7 else { return nil }
    let result = try await TablebaseService.shared.probe(fen: position.consistentFEN)
    return result.moves.first { $0.userVerdict == .keepsWin }?.uci
}

docs.title: Compare your move against the opening explorer
docs.text:
func explorerPopularity(of san: String, in position: Position) async throws -> Double? {
    let result = try await LichessExplorer.shared.explore(fen: position.fen)
    guard let move = result.moves.first(where: { $0.san == san }),
          result.totalGames > 0 else { return nil }
    return Double(move.totalGames) / Double(result.totalGames)
}

docs.title: Import a player's games and prepare them for storage
docs.text:
func importChessCom(username: String) async throws -> [PreparedGameData] {
    let service = ChessAPIService()
    let result = try await service.fetchChessComGames(username: username) { done, total in
        print("archive \(done)/\(total)")
    }
    return result.games.enumerated().map { i, game in
        PreparedGameData(from: game, orderIndex: i)
    }
}

docs.title: Drive a Square-Off desync gate
docs.text:
var gate = SquareOffSyncGate()

func boardSnapshot(outOfSync: Bool, clockRunning: Bool, toMove: PieceColor) {
    switch gate.update(isOutOfSync: outOfSync,
                       clockIsRunning: clockRunning,
                       currentActiveColor: toMove) {
    case .pauseClock:                pauseTheClock()
    case .resumeClock(let color):    resumeTheClock(for: color)
    case .none:                      break
    }
    if gate.shouldFireHaptic {
        playHaptic()
        gate.acknowledgeHaptic()
    }
}

docs.title: Persist a small store over the seam
docs.text:
import FianchettoKit

struct PuzzleProgress: BlobBackedStore {
    static let blobKey = "puzzleProgress"
    var solved: Set<String> = []
    var streak: [Bool] = []
    init() {}
}

let blobStore = MemoryBlobStore()         // your JSONBlobStore implementation
var progress = PuzzleProgress.load(from: blobStore)
progress.solved.insert("puzzle-42")
progress.streak.append(true)
progress.streak.capLast(50)               // keep the most recent 50
progress.save(to: blobStore)

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Wire up a storage backend, then load, mutate, and persist a store.

docs.title: Provide a blob store
docs.text:
FianchettoKit's stat stores don't talk to disk directly — they read and write through the JSONBlobStore seam declared in Storage.swift, so you supply the concrete backend (a database, files, the cloud, or just memory). The simplest backend is an in-memory dictionary:

import FianchettoKit

final class MemoryBlobStore: JSONBlobStore {
    private var storage: [String: String] = [:]
    func loadJSON(forKey key: String) -> String? { storage[key] }
    func saveJSON(_ json: String, forKey key: String) { storage[key] = json }
}

let blobStore = MemoryBlobStore()

A production backend backs saveJSON with a debounced write into a database row (for example a SwiftData/CloudKit row, or a Room row). The store logic doesn't change with the backend.

docs.title: Load, mutate, persist
docs.text:
The Codable stores conform to BlobBackedStore, which gives them load(from:) and save(to:). The mutating record methods persist themselves through the store you pass:

import FianchettoKit

// Tactics Elo — load, record an attempt, get the rating delta back.
var ratings = TacticsRatingStore.load(from: blobStore)
let delta = ratings.recordAttempt(
    puzzleKey: BlunderMasteryStore.key(fen: fen, correctSAN: "Qxh7#"),
    difficulty: .hard,
    outcome: .correct,        // .correct | .wrong | .skipped
    in: blobStore
)
print(ratings.displayUserRating, "(\(delta >= 0 ? "+" : "")\(Int(delta)))")
print(ratings.peakUserRating)

// Per-attempt performance history (accuracy, streaks, timing).
var perf = TacticsPerformanceStore.load(from: blobStore)
perf.record(
    TacticsAttempt(
        puzzleKey: BlunderMasteryStore.key(fen: fen, correctSAN: "Qxh7#"),
        outcome: .correct,
        elapsedSeconds: 8.4,
        attemptOrdinal: 1,
        extractionMode: "punish",
        difficulty: "hard"
    ),
    in: blobStore
)
print(perf.accuracy, perf.currentStreak, perf.bestStreak)

docs.title: The shared key-format contract
docs.text:
Every store that quizzes the user from a flagged position shares one identity string, "<fen>:<correctSAN>". Always build it with BlunderMasteryStore.key(fen:correctSAN:) so the Elo store, the performance store, and the spaced-repetition counter all line up:

let key = BlunderMasteryStore.key(fen: position.fen, correctSAN: "Nf6+")

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: FianchettoKit is a Swift Package Manager library. It depends on ChessCore for the chess model and on BoardKit for the electronic-board kernels and adapters.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Minimum Swift tools 6.0 (Swift 6 language mode) iOS 18.0 macOS 15.0

FianchettoKit targets a higher floor than ChessCore (iOS 13 / macOS 10.15) and includes the networking clients.

docs.title: Add the package
docs.text:
FianchettoKit pulls in ChessCore and BoardKit transitively, so adding it is all you need:

// Package.swift
dependencies: [
    .package(path: "../FianchettoKit"),
],
targets: [
    .target(
        name: "Fianchetto",
        dependencies: [
            .product(name: "FianchettoKit", package: "FianchettoKit"),
        ]
    ),
]

import ChessCore       // Position, MoveGenerator, PGNParser, ...
import FianchettoKit   // JSONBlobStore, BlobBackedStore, the stores, the kernels,
                       // the DTOs, and the network clients

docs.title: The command-line tools
docs.text:
The fianchetto-cli executable lives beside the app at Tools/fianchetto-cli and is a separate SPM package that path-depends on this one, so it is built on its own:

cd Tools/fianchetto-cli
swift build

docs.text:
FianchettoKit ships a DocC catalog and depends on the swift-docc-plugin:

swift package generate-documentation --target FianchettoKit

docs.title: Reconciliation note
docs.text: The FianchettoKit documentation is currently authored across two branches: the library concept pages on one, the fianchetto-cli pages on the other. This note records where each page set lives, the link rule that was followed while they were apart, and exactly what has to happen when they reconcile.

docs.title: The cross-branch link rule that was followed
docs.text:
A page never links to a page that exists only on the other branch. It names it in prose instead.

A Markdown link to a file that is not in docs_dir produces a broken link in the built site and a nav entry that resolves to nothing, so a link written in anticipation of a merge is a defect until the merge lands. Naming the target in prose costs the reader one search and costs the build nothing.

Applied in both directions:

  • The reference-branch pages mention fianchetto-cli and its subcommands eighteen times in prose, and link to a cli/ page zero times.
  • CLI expansion names the reference-branch concept pages in prose and links to none of them, and closes with a note saying why.

The rule has one consequence worth stating: the absence of a link is not a judgement about relevance. Every prose mention listed below is a link that was deliberately withheld, not a connection nobody noticed.

docs.title: Merge task 1 — add the CLI nav section
docs.text:
The reference branch's mkdocs.yml has no Command-Line Interface section, because no cli/ page exists there. The merged config needs one appended after Usage Examples:

  - Command-Line Interface:
      - cli/index.md
      - annotate: cli/annotate.md
      - estimate: cli/estimate.md
      - maia: cli/maia.md
      - accuracy: cli/accuracy.md
      - project: cli/project.md
      - track: cli/track.md
      - Expansion (proposed): cli/expansion.md

Two details that are easy to lose:

  • cli/index.md is listed bare rather than with a title. That is deliberate — the site enables navigation.indexes, so a bare index path makes the section header itself the link to the overview page.
  • cli/expansion.md is not in the CLI branch's nav today. It is reachable only by direct URL. Adding it is part of this task, not a separate one.

Everything else in the two mkdocs.yml files is identical in intent — same theme, same palette, same feature list, same markdown extensions. Take the reference branch's site_description, which does not yet mention the CLI, and extend it.

One mention is not merely unlinked, it is wrong

concepts/network-clients.md:197 reads "This capability is exposed headlessly by the fianchetto-cli import-related subcommands". There are no import subcommands. docs.title: Re-pathing the superseded concept set
docs.text:
The larger job, and the one that breaks the build if skipped. The CLI branch's seven other cli/ pages each close with a "Related" section linking into that branch's own concepts/ directory. Those filenames differ from the reference-branch set, so every one of those links dangles once the reference pages become canonical.

Link in a cli/ page Appears in Retarget to ../concepts/strength-and-elo.md cli/index.md, cli/estimate.md (×2), cli/accuracy.md, cli/project.md, cli/track.md ../concepts/elo-estimation.md ../concepts/engine-annotation.md cli/index.md, cli/annotate.md ../concepts/engine.md ../concepts/maia.md cli/index.md, cli/maia.md ../concepts/engine.md — the reference branch folds Maia into "Engine, Annotation & Maia" ../concepts/analysis.md cli/index.md, cli/accuracy.md ../concepts/analysis.md — unchanged, the only one that survives as-is

One link carries an anchor: cli/estimate.md:133 points at ../concepts/strength-and-elo.md#time-control-routing. The reference page's equivalent section is ## Two time-control classifiers, so the retarget is ../concepts/elo-estimation.md#two-time-control-classifiers. Anchors are generated from heading text, so this one has to be read off the merged page rather than guessed.

Note

Decide the direction before doing any of this. These tables assume the reference-branch concept set wins and the CLI branch's older concepts/ directory is deleted. That is the right call — the reference pages were written against the larger tree and cover subsystems the older set has no page for — but it is a decision, and half-merging the two sets produces two pages describing the same type with different constants.

docs.title: Merge-day checklist
docs.text:
1. Choose the concept set. The reference-branch pages win; delete the CLI
   branch's concepts/ directory rather than merging it page by page.
2. Copy the cli/ directory onto the reference branch unchanged.
3. Append the Command-Line Interface nav section to mkdocs.yml, including
   cli/expansion.md, and extend site_description to mention the CLI.
4. Retarget the four ../concepts/ link paths in the seven older cli/ pages,
   including the one anchor.
5. Correct concepts/network-clients.md:197 — the import subcommands are
   proposed, not shipped — then link it to cli/expansion.md.
6. Link the other seventeen prose CLI mentions in the concept pages.
7. Link the prose concept mentions in cli/expansion.md and delete its
   closing cross-branch admonition.
8. Build with strict link checking. Every item above is a dangling link if
   it is missed, so the build is the acceptance test.
9. Delete this note, or reduce it to a dated changelog entry.

Step 8 is the one that makes the rest safe. Every task on this page is either adding a link or repointing one, so a build that fails on unresolved links catches anything skipped — which is the reason the link rule was worth following while the branches were apart.

docs.title: fianchetto-cli
docs.text: Six headless subcommands that expose Fianchetto's engine and analysis seams as stdin/stdout filters. Every command reads one JSON object per line and writes one JSON object per line, so an entire library can be annotated, scored, tracked, and projected from a shell pipeline.

docs.title: Why it exists
docs.text:
The CLI is not a reimplementation. Its Package.swift depends on the same path-pinned packages the app builds against, so a number printed by fianchetto-cli is the number the app would have computed for that input:

Dependency Path What it supplies FianchettoKit ../../FianchettoKit AnnotationKernel, AnnotationDriver, AccuracyAggregator, EloEstimator, StrengthTracker, both calibrators, MaiaBackfillPolicy, Maia3Encoding ChessCore ../../../ChessCore (sibling @ 7fdb0d1) Position, Game, PGNParser, UCIParser, UCIOutputParser, MoveQuality SwiftStockfish ../../../SwiftStockfish (sibling @ 05ec038) the in-process Stockfish the app ships, plus the NNUE manifest

Two words are used throughout these pages, and they mean precise things:

  • Linked — the CLI calls the app's own shipped code. The behavior cannot drift, because there is only one copy.
  • Mirrored — the logic lives in the app target rather than a library, so an SPM executable cannot import it. It is reproduced in the CLI with file:line citations to the original.
Command Linked Mirrored estimate everything numerical nothing (JSON shaping only) accuracy everything numerical nothing (JSON shaping only) track everything numerical nothing (JSON shaping only) project tracker + both calibrators the StatsKernel.eloPoints wiring order maia grid, conditioning, qualification, encoding, log-softmax the Core ML transport and the grid-sweep loop annotate kernel, driver, parsers, FEN sanitizer, engine, nets manifest, movetime policy, White-POV math the UCI session plumbing

Only two commands mirror anything load-bearing, and both for the same reason: the app's EngineManager and MaiaEngine are @MainActor, @Observable-coupled, and entangled with SwiftData, UserDefaults, and thermal gates. Everything that decides a number still comes from the kit.

docs.title: Building and running
docs.text:
The package is tools-only — swift-tools-version: 6.0, Swift 6 language mode, a macOS 15 floor inherited from FianchettoKit, one executable product. The app's own project is untouched.

cd Tools/fianchetto-cli
swift build
.build/debug/fianchetto-cli <command> [options] < input.jsonl > output.jsonl

Two defaults are resolved relative to #filePath — the annotate NNUE directory and the Maia model package, both under <repo>/Fianchetto/Resources. A binary copied away from this checkout must pass --nets-dir / --model-path.

docs.title: The commands
docs.text: Command Produces Wraps annotate per-ply White-POV centipawn evals the app's Stockfish annotation path estimate a per-game Elo performance + CI EloEstimator.estimate maia the 11-point Maia log-likelihood evidence vector MaiaBackfillPolicy + Maia3Encoding accuracy per-move losses, labels, and both accuracy aggregates AccuracyAggregator project the serving-side strength point for one account pool StatsKernel.eloPoints's wiring track the Kalman strength posterior after each game StrengthTracker

docs.title: The JSON-Lines protocol
docs.text:
One JSONLines enum owns the whole contract, so all six commands behave identically at the stream level.

stdin
    read with readLine, one request per line
    blank / whitespace-only line   -> skipped, no output
    decodes for this command       -> one response line
    fails to decode                -> {"error": "unparseable request line: <underlying>"}
                                      and the stream CONTINUES

stdout
    JSONEncoder outputFormatting = [.sortedKeys, .withoutEscapingSlashes]
    one object per line, in input order, flushed immediately
    keys are alphabetical (stable golden diffs)
    nil fields are omitted entirely, not written as null

stderr
    every human-readable diagnostic: engine identity, model load, ANE probe
    verdicts, self-test PASS/FAIL. Never mixed into stdout.

Two consequences of "nil fields are omitted" are worth knowing before you write a consumer: an error line for a request whose id could not be read has no id key at all, and project's projection key is absent — not null — until the anchored calibrator has warmed up.

A per-request failure is a data event, not a process event: the command emits {"id": …, "error": …} for that line and moves on. The one exception is annotate, where a wedged engine aborts the whole run (see that page).

Because output is flushed per line and input order is preserved, the binary can be driven as a long-lived pipe rather than re-spawned per game — which matters most for annotate (one engine handshake per run) and maia (one model compile per run).

docs.title: Dispatch, help, and exit codes
docs.text:
Situation Output Exit no arguments global help on stdout 2 first argument is -h, --help, or help global help on stdout 0 unknown command token fianchetto-cli: unknown command '<token>' on stderr, then global help 2 --help / -h anywhere after the command token that command's usage 0 the command throws fianchetto-cli <name>: <error> on stderr 1 normal completion the response stream 0

The global help pads each command name to 12 characters before its abstract, and the registry order is the listing order: annotate, estimate, maia, accuracy, project, track.

docs.title: Composing the commands
docs.text:
Hop Flows through untouched Needs reshaping annotate → accuracy id, white_pov_evals add start_is_white, color annotate → estimate id, white_pov_evals add start_is_white, color, clock fields estimate → track the whole object (extra keys are ignored) nothing estimate → project elo, ci_low, ci_high, accuracy, sample_moves wrap as performance, add actual_rating maia → estimate maia_log_likes or build a maia_evidence object from maia_log_likes + positions_scored + opponent_conditioning 
fianchetto-cli annotate < games.jsonl       > evals.jsonl
# join each row with its start_is_white / color / clock fields first
fianchetto-cli estimate < estimate-in.jsonl > estimates.jsonl
fianchetto-cli track    < estimates.jsonl   > posterior.jsonl

track and project both consume an ordered sequence: oldest game first. project additionally models exactly one account pool per run — grouping by provider × account × speed stays with the caller, exactly as StatsKernel does it.

docs.title: Adding a subcommand
docs.text:
The subcommand seam is four requirements and one array. This is the entire protocol:

protocol CLICommand: Sendable {
    /// The subcommand token, e.g. `"annotate"` in `fianchetto-cli annotate`.
    static var name: String { get }
    /// One-line description for `fianchetto-cli --help`.
    static var abstract: String { get }
    /// Usage text (flags + stdin/stdout contract) for `<command> --help`.
    static var usage: String { get }
    /// Run with the arguments AFTER the subcommand token.
    static func run(arguments: [String]) async throws
}

var commandRegistry: [any CLICommand.Type] {
    [
        AnnotateCommand.self,
        EstimateCommand.self,
        MaiaCommand.self,
        AccuracyCommand.self,
        ProjectCommand.self,
        TrackCommand.self,
    ]
}

Adding a command is one new file plus one line in commandRegistry. Main needs no change: it already handles dispatch, --help, and mapping a thrown error to exit code 1.

The shared I/O helpers are the rest of the skeleton:

struct ExampleCommand: CLICommand {
    static let name = "example"
    static let abstract = "one line, shown in the global help table"
    static let usage = "USAGE: fianchetto-cli example < in.jsonl > out.jsonl\n…"

    struct Request: Decodable {
        let id: String
        let whitePovEvals: [Double]
        enum CodingKeys: String, CodingKey {
            case id
            case whitePovEvals = "white_pov_evals"   // explicit snake_case
        }
    }

    struct Response: Encodable { let id: String; let value: Double }

    static func run(arguments: [String]) async throws {
        guard arguments.isEmpty else {
            throw CLIError("unknown option '\(arguments[0])' (see: fianchetto-cli example --help)")
        }
        await JSONLines.forEachRequest(Request.self) { result in
            switch result {
            case .failure(let failure):
                JSONLines.emitRawError(id: nil, message: "unparseable request line: \(failure.underlying)")
            case .success(let request):
                JSONLines.emit(Response(id: request.id, value: 0))
            }
        }
    }
}

Conventions the six existing commands all follow:

  • Codable wire types with explicit snake_case CodingKeys — never rely on a key-decoding strategy, so the contract is readable in one place.
  • An options loop that rejects unknown flags by name, pointing at fianchetto-cli <name> --help.
  • Per-line error isolation through JSONLines.emitRawError; only an unrecoverable process-level failure throws.
  • JSONLines.note for diagnostics — stdout stays machine-readable.
  • A self-test or an always-on sanity oracle wherever the seam permits one: estimate has --self-test (15 golden-parity checks), and maia runs a fail-closed start-position probe on every invocation.

docs.title: accuracy
docs.text: Per-move win-probability losses, per-move accuracies, quality labels, band counts with their ply indices, phase splits, and both game-accuracy aggregates — for one side, from a White-POV eval array. Every formula is a linked AccuracyAggregator call; the command only shapes JSON.

docs.title: stdin
docs.text:
One JSON object per line.

Field Type Required Default Meaning id String yes — echoed on the response line white_pov_evals [Double] yes — the annotate output array; needs at least 2 entries start_is_white Bool yes — which color moved at ply 0 color String yes — "white" or "black", case-insensitive; whose moves are graded

There are no optional fields.

docs.title: stdout
docs.text:
Field Type Meaning id String the request id accuracy Double per-move-average accuracy — the number the app's Review pane shows accuracy_mean_loss Double mean-loss aggregate — what calibration and EloEstimator use sample_moves Int how many moves this side made move_plies [Int] 0-based ply index of each of this side's moves move_wp_losses [Double] per-move win-probability drop, mover POV, on the 0…1 scale move_accuracies [Double] per-move accuracy, 0…100 move_qualities [String] "best" / "excellent" / "good" / "inaccuracy" / "mistake" / "blunder" blunders, mistakes, inaccuracies Int band-exclusive counts, not cumulative blunder_plies, mistake_plies, inaccuracy_plies [Int] the plies behind those counts phase_accuracy [String: Double] keyed opening / middlegame / endgame, over the phases this side actually played

The four parallel arrays (move_plies, move_wp_losses, move_accuracies, move_qualities) are index-aligned and always have sample_moves entries.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: None at all. Any argument is an error, including an unrecognized one — --help and -h are intercepted by the dispatcher before the command runs.

docs.title: The formulas
docs.text:
All constants live in AccuracyAggregator and appear nowhere else in the codebase:

winProbability(cp) = 1 / (1 + exp(-0.00368208 * cp))

mover POV        wp        for white
                 1 - wp    for black
wpDrop_i         = max(0, wpBefore_i - wpAfter_i)              // 0…1
moveAccuracy_i   = clamp(103.1668 * exp(-0.04354 * (wpDrop_i * 100)) - 3.1668, 0, 100)

accuracy             = mean(moveAccuracy_i)                    // per-move average
accuracy_mean_loss   = clamp(103.1668 * exp(-0.04354 * meanLoss) - 3.1668, 0, 100)
    where meanLoss   = mean(min(100, wpDrop_i * 100))

The two aggregates differ by more than rounding. Applying a convex curve to each move and then averaging is not the same as averaging the losses and applying the curve once — by Jensen's inequality the per-move average is always the higher of the two. Both are emitted because both are load-bearing: the Review pane shows the first, and every calibration row was labeled with the second, so mixing them would silently bias every Elo estimate.

Labels come from the same win-probability drop:

classifyMoveQuality(wpDrop:playedBestMove:)
    playedBestMove   -> .best        // never fires here
    wpDrop >= 0.20   -> .blunder
    wpDrop >= 0.10   -> .mistake
    wpDrop >= 0.05   -> .inaccuracy
    wpDrop >= 0.02   -> .good
    else             -> .excellent

playedBestMove is hardwired false in this command. An eval array carries no best-move identity — knowing the position was worth +43 before and +35 after says nothing about which move the engine preferred — so the .best override cannot be evaluated here. The app applies it only where best-move UCIs are stored alongside the evals. A move labeled "best" therefore never appears in this command's output.

Counting is band-exclusive: a blunder is not also counted as a mistake and an inaccuracy. Sum the three fields to get "moves worse than good".

Phases split by full move number, derived as (ply / 2) + 1:

moves  1–10  -> opening
moves 11–30  -> middlegame
moves 31+    -> endgame

A phase key is absent when this side made no moves in it — callers should skip it rather than read it as 0.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: An unknown color, an array with fewer than 2 entries, a side that made no moves in the array, or a nil return from AccuracyAggregator.accuracy(evalsJSON:…) each emit {"id", "error"} and continue.

docs.title: Worked example
docs.text:
Taking the Scholar's-mate eval array straight from annotate and grading Black:

printf '%s\n' \
  '{"id":"scholars-mate","white_pov_evals":[43,35,35,-59,-40,-46,100000,100000],"start_is_white":true,"color":"black"}' \
  | .build/debug/fianchetto-cli accuracy

{"accuracy":66.3538,"accuracy_mean_loss":42.6294,"blunder_plies":[5],"blunders":1,
 "id":"scholars-mate","inaccuracies":0,"inaccuracy_plies":[],"mistake_plies":[],"mistakes":0,
 "move_accuracies":[100,92.4963,6.5652],"move_plies":[1,3,5],
 "move_qualities":["excellent","excellent","blunder"],
 "move_wp_losses":[0,0.0173437,0.5422430],
 "phase_accuracy":{"opening":66.3538},"sample_moves":3}

(Floats are rounded here for width; the real line carries full double precision and is emitted as a single line.) Ply 5 is Nf6??, allowing mate: the win-probability drop of 0.54 is well past the 0.20 blunder threshold and drives the per-move accuracy to 6.6. Note how far the two aggregates separate on a short game with one catastrophe — 66.35 per-move-average against 42.63 mean-loss. Grading White on the same array instead reports one inaccuracy at ply 2 and an overall 90.50.

docs.title: Seam provenance
docs.text:
Fully linked to AccuracyAggregator:

Behavior Kit surface the logistic AccuracyAggregator.winProbability(cp:) per-move accuracy AccuracyAggregator.moveAccuracy(wpBefore:wpAfter:) per-move-average accuracy, phases, sample counts AccuracyAggregator.accuracy(evalsJSON:startIsWhite:color:) mean-loss aggregate AccuracyAggregator.accuracy(fromMeanLoss:) labels AccuracyAggregator.classifyMoveQuality(wpDrop:playedBestMove:) the label strings themselves ChessCore MoveQuality raw values

Nothing is mirrored. The per-move sweep the command runs to build the parallel arrays uses the identical mover-POV flip and wpDrop convention as the kit's own accuracy(evalsJSON:) walk, and the game-level number is taken from that kit call rather than recomputed — the arrays and the scalar cannot disagree.

guard let gameAccuracy = AccuracyAggregator.accuracy(
    evalsJSON: evalsJSON,          // white-POV centipawns, plies + 1 entries
    startIsWhite: true,
    color: .black
), let overall = gameAccuracy.overall else { return }

gameAccuracy.phases[.opening]      // nil when the side made no moves in that phase
gameAccuracy.overallSampleCount

docs.title: annotate
docs.text: Per-ply White-POV centipawn evals for arbitrary games, produced by driving a live UCI Stockfish session through the app's own annotation sweep. This is the command that turns games into the white_pov_evals array every other command consumes.

docs.title: stdin
docs.text:
One JSON object per line.

Field Type Required Default Meaning id String yes — echoed on the response line; the only unconditionally required field uci_moves [String] one of the two — moves from the standard start position, resolved strictly through UCIParser.uciToMove pgn String one of the two — a PGN game; headers optional movetime_ms Int no the thoroughness policy below engine movetime per position thoroughness String no "default" behavior "fast" / "default" / "thorough" — the app's annotation-thoroughness scale

If both uci_moves and pgn are present, uci_moves wins. A game with zero main-line moves is an error, not an empty result.

Movetime, when movetime_ms is absent, comes from AnnotationKernel.annotateMovetime(batch: true, thoroughness:) — integer arithmetic on the batch base:

base = 500 ms                     (batch; the single-game base of 1000 is not used here)
"fast"      -> base * 6 / 10   =  300 ms
"thorough"  -> base * 16 / 10  =  800 ms
"default", null, anything else -> 500 ms

docs.title: stdout
docs.text:
One JSON object per line, in input order.

Field Type Meaning id String the request id white_pov_evals [Double] length = plies + 1; [0] is the start position and [i + 1] is the position after ply i engine.name String the engine's own id name line from the UCI handshake engine.version String parsed from that name: the first digit-bearing token onward, joined by spaces ("Stockfish 18" → "18"); empty when absent engine.options [String: String] the setoption values this session applied

engine.options always carries Threads and Hash. It also carries nnue — the required NNUE sha256s, sorted and joined with + — but only when the in-process engine is used. MultiPV is re-sent before every search and is deliberately not recorded there.

Evals are always oriented to White: positive means White is better regardless of whose turn it is. Forced mates flatten to ±100000, the app's sentinel; a terminal checkmate position is filled by the driver as -100000 from the mover's point of view and converted to White POV by the kernel. Stalemate fills as 0.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Meaning Default --engine-path <path> drive an external UCI binary over stdin/stdout pipes the in-process SwiftStockfish the app ships — not a system or Homebrew Stockfish --nets-dir <dir> NNUE directory for the in-process engine <repo>/Fianchetto/Resources, located by walking five parents up from #filePath --threads <n> engine Threads; must parse as an Int ≥ 1 max(1, ProcessInfo.processInfo.activeProcessorCount / 2)

There is no --hash flag. Hash follows from threads, exactly as the app derives it:

threads >= 4 -> Hash 256 MB
threads >= 2 -> Hash 128 MB
otherwise    ->  Hash 64 MB

A --nets-dir that fails StockfishNetworkLoader.requiredNetworksSatisfied(in:) is rejected with a message naming the required filenames, and any unrecognized argument is a hard error.

docs.title: The engine session
docs.text:
The per-position protocol is the app's, step for step, with the budgets it uses:

handshake (once)
    "uci" -> capture `id name` / `id author` until "uciok"      budget 20 s
    setoption name Threads value <n>
    setoption name Hash value <mb>
    "isready" -> "readyok"                                      budget 20 s

pre-run barrier (ONCE per process, not per game — the transposition table
deliberately carries across games of one run)
    "stop" + "isready"                                          budget 30 s
    "ucinewgame" + "isready"                                    budget 30 s

per position
    setoption name MultiPV value 2
    position fen <Position.stockfishSafeFEN>
    go movetime <ms>
    safety timeout = max(30, movetime / 1000 * 4) seconds       (integer division)

The info accumulation rule is the subtle part, and it is the app's rule verbatim:

a line must carry a score to be considered at all
a pv-less line never displaces a pv-bearing entry at the same MultiPV rank
a score-bearing pv-less line still fills an empty slot
    -> this is what makes terminal `info depth 0 score mate 0` work

"bestmove" ends the search; "bestmove (none)" parses to nil and becomes ""
rank-1 score presence still gates the result inside AnnotationKernel.extractEval

On a safety timeout the CLI sends stop, drains that search's terminal bestmove with a 5-second budget, and returns nil — which makes AnnotationDriver abort the sweep, exactly like the app's "engine stopped responding" path.

docs.title: Failure semantics
docs.text: Failure Effect unparseable line {"error": …}, stream continues illegal UCI move, unparseable PGN, no moves, neither input field {"id", "error"} for that game, stream continues the engine stops responding {"id", "error": "engine stopped responding"}, remaining stdin lines are drained without processing, process exits 1

docs.title: Worked example
docs.text:
printf '%s\n' \
  '{"id": "scholars-mate", "uci_moves": ["e2e4","e7e5","d1h5","b8c6","f1c4","g8f6","h5f7"], "movetime_ms": 120}' \
  | .build/debug/fianchetto-cli annotate --threads 1

{"engine":{"name":"Stockfish 18","options":{"Hash":"64","Threads":"1","nnue":"37f18f62…+c288c895…"},"version":"18"},"id":"scholars-mate","white_pov_evals":[43,35,35,-59,-40,-46,100000,100000]}

Seven plies in, eight evals out. The mate-in-one after ply 6 and the checkmate position itself both pin to +100000; the fool's-mate mirror (f2f3 e7e5 g2g4 d8h4) pins to -100000. The nnue sha256s are elided above for width — the real line carries them in full.

docs.title: Seam provenance
docs.text:
Linked — everything that decides a number:

Behavior Kit surface the eval sweep, including the terminal-position fill and abort-on-failure AnnotationDriver.collectEvals(positions:evaluator:) checkmate -100000 / stalemate 0 sentinels AnnotationKernel.terminalEval(for:) rank-1/rank-2 resolution, mate → ±100000, nil when rank 1 is scoreless AnnotationKernel.extractEval(fromRankedInfos:bestMoveUCI:) movetime / thoroughness policy AnnotationKernel.annotateMovetime(batch:thoroughness:) engine-POV → White-POV conversion AnnotationKernel.whitePovEvals(_:startIsWhite:) FEN sanitization, UCI/PGN parsing, info parsing ChessCore Position.stockfishSafeFEN, UCIParser, Game.loadPGN, UCIOutputParser the engine and its NNUE manifest SwiftStockfish StockfishEngine, StockfishNetworks

Mirrored — the UCI session plumbing only (UCIAnnotationSession.swift): handshake, option application, the pre-run barrier, the accumulation rules above, the safety timeout, and a generation-guarded line mailbox so a stale timer can never resume a later wait. The app's EngineManager lives in the app target, is @MainActor and @Observable-coupled, and is entangled with SwiftData, UserDefaults, thermal gates, and stream leases, so an SPM executable cannot import it.

PositionEvaluator conformance is the load-bearing seam: the CLI's session implements evaluate(fen:) async -> AnnotationEval?, which is what lets the kit's own sweep drive it.

// What the CLI does, in kit terms:
let positions = [game.startPosition] + game.mainLine.map(\.positionAfter)
guard let evals = await AnnotationDriver.collectEvals(
    positions: positions,
    evaluator: session           // any PositionEvaluator
) else { /* engine stopped responding */ return }

let whitePovEvals = AnnotationKernel.whitePovEvals(
    evals,
    startIsWhite: game.startPosition.activeColor == .white
)

Intentional, output-neutral differences from the app: searches are strictly sequential (no stale-bestmove bookkeeping needed); no MultiPV startup seed, since annotation re-sends MultiPV 2 before every search anyway; no thermal or background pause gate and no persistence; thoroughness comes from the request instead of UserDefaults; bestmove (none) ends the search immediately; and zero-move or unparseable games emit an explicit error line instead of being stamped unevaluable.

docs.title: estimate
docs.text: Turns one game's White-POV eval array — plus its clock, and optionally Maia evidence and the PGN Termination tag — into a calibrated per-game Elo performance with a confidence interval. Everything numerical is linked kit code; the command adds JSON shaping and one route label.

docs.title: stdin
docs.text:
One JSON object per line.

Field Type Required Default Meaning id String yes — echoed on the response line white_pov_evals [Double] yes — the annotate output array; needs at least 2 entries start_is_white Bool yes — which color moved at ply 0 color String yes — "white" or "black", case-insensitive; which side is being rated tc_base_seconds Int or null no null base clock; null means correspondence tc_increment_seconds Int or null no treated as 0 per-move increment is_otb_classical Bool no false widens the CI by 1.5× maia_log_likes [Double] no absent legacy bare 11-point vector maia_evidence object no absent versioned evidence; takes precedence over the bare vector termination String no absent PGN Termination value; feeds the is_time feature

maia_evidence has three required members:

Member Type Meaning log_likes [Double] the 11-point vector eligible_move_count Int how many owner moves were scored opponent_conditioning String exactly "exact-lichess-opponent" or "neutral-lichess-1500"

docs.title: stdout
docs.text:
Field Type Meaning id String the request id elo Double point estimate, clamped to 100…3500 ci_low / ci_high Double the interval; not re-clamped, so a floored estimate can report a lower bound below 100 below_floor Bool the raw model output fell below the calibration floor route String "v41-ensemble" / "v41-no-maia" / "v2-correspondence" serving_path String "exactOpponentMaiaEnsemble" / "neutral1500EvidenceExactArtifact" / "moveQualityFallback" accuracy Double 0–100, the mean-loss aggregate (not the Review pane's per-move average) sample_moves Int this side's move count

route and serving_path answer different questions. route names the artifact that served the game; serving_path names the evidence that reached it, and is the raw value of EloEstimatorServingPath:

Input route serving_path correspondence (tc_base_seconds: null) v2-correspondence moveQualityFallback — the v2 lookup never consumes Maia evidence typed evidence, exact-lichess-opponent v41-ensemble exactOpponentMaiaEnsemble typed evidence, neutral-lichess-1500 v41-ensemble neutral1500EvidenceExactArtifact legacy bare maia_log_likes v41-ensemble exactOpponentMaiaEnsemble no evidence, or evidence that fails validation v41-no-maia moveQualityFallback

Evidence fails validation — and silently demotes to the no-Maia ridge — when the vector length is not 11, when any log-like is non-finite, or when typed evidence reports eligible_move_count <= 0.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Meaning Default --self-test run the golden-parity fixtures and exit without reading stdin off

That is the only flag. When it is absent the argument list must be empty, or the command errors.

docs.title: Decision rules
docs.text:
Time-control class selects the artifact, and a null base is the correspondence signal:

TimeControlClass.classify(baseSeconds:incrementSeconds:)
    baseSeconds == nil -> .correspondence
    total = baseSeconds + 40 * incrementSeconds
    total <  180 -> .bullet        total < 1500 -> .rapid
    total <  480 -> .blitz         else         -> .classical

Correspondence has no v4.1 model at all, so estimate falls through to the v2 binned-median lookup on accuracy alone — that is what route: "v2-correspondence" records.

The interval is built the same way on both branches:

pointElo     = clamp(rawElo, 100.0, 3500.0)
below_floor  = rawElo < 100.0                     // v4.1 branch
sampleFactor = min(3.0, sqrt(max(1.0, 20.0 / nMoves)))
otbFactor    = is_otb_classical ? 1.5 : 1.0
halfWidth    = baseHalfWidth * sampleFactor * otbFactor

baseHalfWidth
    below floor -> 2.0 * the first residual band's MAE
    otherwise   -> the residual std for pointElo in the serving artifact

On the v2 branch below_floor means something different: accuracy fell below the lowest binned center and the lookup clamped. The same 2× MAE widening applies.

Note

sampleFactor is 1.0 for any game of 20 or more owner moves. A game with fewer than 3 owner moves returns an error rather than an estimate, so on the v4.1 branch the factor reaches at most sqrt(20/3) ≈ 2.58 and the 3.0 cap never binds.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: An unknown color, an opponent_conditioning string that is not one of the two accepted values, or a nil return from EloEstimator (fewer than 2 evals, or fewer than 3 moves by this side) each emit {"id", "error"} and continue.

docs.title: Worked example
docs.text:
printf '%s\n' \
  '{"id":"g1","white_pov_evals":[0,-54.5,-12.0,-140.2,-60.1,-58.0,-210.4,-190.0,-33.0,-40.0,-28.0],"start_is_white":true,"color":"white","tc_base_seconds":300,"tc_increment_seconds":5,"termination":"time forfeit"}' \
  | .build/debug/fianchetto-cli estimate

The response line carries these keys, alphabetically ordered by the encoder:

{"accuracy":79.8,"below_floor":false,"ci_high":1833.0,"ci_low":1571.0,"elo":1702.0,"id":"g1","route":"v41-no-maia","sample_moves":30,"serving_path":"moveQualityFallback"}

(Values are illustrative — the shape and key set are exact.) 300 + 40 × 5 = 500 routes this game through the rapid artifact even though Chess.com would rate it as blitz; see Time-control routing.

To use Maia evidence, attach the object maia produces:

{"id":"g1","white_pov_evals":[…],"start_is_white":true,"color":"white","tc_base_seconds":300,"tc_increment_seconds":5,"maia_evidence":{"log_likes":[-15.07,-13.45,-12.56,-12.17,-12.19,-11.36,-11.79,-11.96,-11.93,-12.55,-13.17],"eligible_move_count":3,"opponent_conditioning":"exact-lichess-opponent"}}

docs.title: --self-test
docs.text:
--self-test runs eight synthetic fixtures through the same response(for:) function the stream path uses, checks fifteen properties, writes [PASS] / [FAIL] lines to stderr, and exits 0 only if all fifteen pass. Any failure throws, listing the failing check names, and exits 1.

The fixtures are a port of EloEstimatorGoldenTests.syntheticEvalArray:

k       = 0.00368208
cpDown  = -ln(100 / (50 - lossPct) - 1) / k
evals[0] = 0;  odd plies = cpDown;  even plies = 0

All eight are 60 plies, White, start_is_white: true:

Fixture Clock Loss Extra rapid_5pct 600+0 5 % — classical_5pct_nomaia 1800+0 5 % — classical_5pct_maia_uniform 1800+0 5 % an 11-long vector of -100.0 blitz_40pct 300+0 40 % — classical_5pct_base 5400+30 5 % — classical_5pct_otb 5400+30 5 % is_otb_classical corr_5pct null / null 5 % — rapid_via_increment 300+10 5 % —

The fifteen checks:

# Check 1 rapid elo within 50 of 1702 2 rapid not below_floor 3 rapid CI half-width > 50 4 rapid route is v41-no-maia 5 classical no-Maia elo within 50 of 1665 6 uniform-Maia classical elo within 50 of 971 7 uniform-Maia classical route is v41-ensemble 8 40 %-loss blitz clamps to within 1.0 of 100 9 that game is flagged below_floor 10 that game's CI half-width > 300 11 OTB / non-OTB CI half-width ratio is 1.5 within 0.01 12 OTB point estimate is unchanged, within 0.01 13 correspondence elo within 10 of 1886.75 14 correspondence route is v2-correspondence 15 300 + 40 × 10 = 700 routes to rapid: elo and ci_low exactly equal the 600+0 case

Check 15 is the one that would catch a silent change to the banding rule: two different clocks that must produce bit-identical output.

docs.title: Seam provenance
docs.text:
Fully linked. The command calls EloEstimator.estimate(whitePovEvals:startIsWhite:color:tc:isOTBClassical:maiaLogLikes:maiaEvidence:termination:) — the same overload StatsKernel serves from — with TimeControlClass.classify(baseSeconds:incrementSeconds:) for routing and MaiaBackfillPolicy.TargetEvidence / OpponentConditioning for the typed evidence. Nothing is mirrored; the only CLI-original logic is the three-way route label.

let tc = TimeControlClass.classify(baseSeconds: 300, incrementSeconds: 5)

guard let performance = EloEstimator.estimate(
    whitePovEvals: whitePovEvals,
    startIsWhite: true,
    color: .white,
    tc: tc,
    isOTBClassical: false,
    maiaLogLikes: nil,
    maiaEvidence: MaiaBackfillPolicy.TargetEvidence(
        logLikes: logLikes,
        eligibleMoveCount: 3,
        opponentConditioning: .exactLichess
    ),
    termination: "time forfeit"
) else { return }

performance.elo
performance.ci                 // ClosedRange<Double>
performance.servingPath        // .exactOpponentMaiaEnsemble
performance.belowCalibrationFloor

docs.title: CLI expansion (proposed)
docs.text:
fianchetto-cli runs the app's own validated logic headlessly, so every FianchettoKit seam that decides a number without a view attached is a candidate for a subcommand. This page ranks the candidates a full survey of the kit turned up, sketches wire contracts for the strongest, and records which seams are honestly not worth exposing.

Everything on this page is a proposal

The CLI implements exactly six subcommands today: annotate, estimate, maia, accuracy, project, track. Nothing below is implemented. Command names are proposals and may change; the seams are real and every signature, argument label, and constant quoted here was read out of the kit source.

docs.title: Why expand at all
docs.text:
The CLI is not a reimplementation — it links the same package the app builds against, so a number it prints is the number the app would have computed. That property is what makes a subcommand worth more than a script, and it buys four things a running app cannot:

What it buys Research throughput Corpus-scale answers — feature matrices, yield counts, distributions, inference budgets — over a library instead of one game at a time Batch QA A pass/fail gate over a fixture directory that a CI job can run, rather than a manual sweep through a UI Regression baselines A golden output file, diffable on every change, pinning a constant that today only a running app exercises App parity One canonical answer both the Apple and Android shells can diff against, instead of two independent derivations that drift

The fourth is the one with a track record. Several kernels in the kit exist because the two shells disagreed, and their source comments name the divergence they were extracted to kill. A CLI turns each of those from a one-time fix into a standing check.

docs.title: What counts as a candidate
docs.text:
A seam qualifies when three things hold at once: it is public, it is a function of values a JSON line (or a PGN) can reconstruct, and it has a consumer that is not a view. The third test eliminates most of the kit — a great deal of it decides a label or a color for exactly one SwiftUI surface, and a subcommand around that is a maintenance liability rather than a capability.

Candidates are ranked by value over effort, both scored on stated ladders so the ordering can be argued with:

rank = (research value + QA/parity value) / implementation effort

research value  corpus-scale answers the app cannot give — feature matrices,
                distributions, inference budgets, dataset generation,
                train/test hygiene
QA value        Apple/Android parity, golden fixtures, and regression pinning of
                a constant that today only a running app can exercise

effort  1  public pure statics over scalars, strings, and value types;
           JSON plumbing only
        2  needs a PGN replay (ChessCore Position / MoveGenerator), a
           multi-field nested request object, or a filesystem shim
        3  needs the MoveNode / Game object graph, a bundled resource, or
           the network
        4  needs an engine process, a tablebase service, or a Maia
           inference backend
        X  blocked — the seam is not public

Effort 1 and 2 is the interesting band. Everything at effort 4 already has a precedent in annotate and maia, and it is a precedent that costs an engine handshake or a model compile per run.

docs.title: Tier 1 — build these first
docs.text:
Eight proposals where the ratio is not close. All are effort 1 or 2, and each answers a question that today requires launching an app.

# Proposed command Seam it wraps What it unlocks Effort Value 1 chart EloChartPresentation.domain(points:showsComparableRating:), .displayedInterval(for:), .unclippedPerformance(for:), .clipped(_:to:) A reference Y-domain and per-point clip both shells diff against. This is the only candidate whose bug class has already shipped and been measured 2 very high (QA) 2 classify TimeControlClass.classify(baseSeconds:incrementSeconds:), .classify(fromPGNTag:), StatsKernel.classifySpeed(tags:event:), .parseTags(_:), .startsWithWhiteToMove(tags:) Every derived bucket for one game per line, including the deliberate estimator/rating-pool disagreement that decides which artifact serves a game 1 high (QA) 3 identity GameIdentity.canonicalProviderID(_:), .stableID(gameID:link:site:contentID:), .isRecognizedOnlineGameLocation(_:), GameDedup.compositeKey(...) Production identity rules for any external ingest, including this project's own corpus builders. Stops a duplicate game leaking across a train/test split 1 high (research) 4 combo CombinationMiningKernel.candidates(from:), .candidates(in:userIsWhite:), .validateLine(startingFEN:uciMoves:), .score(naiveCp:seeCp:evalCp:sharpnessCp:foundIt:), .staticExchangeEvaluation(move:in:) Stage 1 is pure and engine-free, so a whole library mines offline in seconds. Retune six named thresholds against measured candidate counts without waiting on Stockfish 1 high (research) 5 tactics TacticsExtractor.extract(from:mode:mateMaxN:swingThreshold:), .extractAll(from:modes:mateMaxN:swingThreshold:) Puzzle yield per extraction mode over a corpus at zero engine cost, and labeled puzzle-dataset generation for offline evaluation 1 high (research) 6 glyphs AnnotationKernel.computeAnnotations(inputs:evals:startIsWhite:), .classifyGlyph(...), .involvesSacrifice(positionBefore:positionAfter:) Re-runs the glyph threshold cascade against a frozen eval corpus, so threshold tuning iterates in seconds instead of an engine sweep 2 high (QA) 7 store FileJSONBlobStore.storedJSONKeysReportingError(maximumKeys:), .loadJSONReportingError(forKey:), .snapshotJSONByKey(excludingKeys:includingAuthoredRecords:), .validateEndgameMiningRoute(forKey:), .storedAuthoredJSONKeysReportingError(...) Makes a blob directory a debuggable artifact, and is the enabler for every stateful proposal below — see the storage seam 1 medium-high (QA) 8 reconcile LibraryGameReconciliation.plan(games:) over [LibraryBackup.Game] Dry-run the exact planner that runs before a destructive "remove duplicates" action, against a real exported backup, with no persistence attached 1 high (both)

store ranks seventh on its own merits and higher on leverage: merge-progress, progress, authored, and the endgame generation validators all need a file-backed blob directory, and it is the command that makes one inspectable.

docs.text:
Effort 1–2, no engine, no network. Each is a day or less and pins something that is currently only reachable through a running app.
