startSession(boardBrandRawValue:) resets the buffer and seeds a comment eboard-diag v1 brand=<raw> at offset 0. appendRaw(bytes:) hex-encodes and skips an empty frame; appendLifecycle(_:) and annotate(_:) take strings. Timestamps are relative by construction — sessionStartTimestamp is stored but never exported.

asReplayText()

# eboard-diag capture (field diagnostics)
# board: <boardBrandRawValue>          (line omitted when empty)
# privacy: content-only (board frames + moves; no player names, no device ID, relative timestamps)
<blank line>

per entry, in capture order:
  .comment   -> "# <data>"                          (does not advance lastOffsetMs)
  .lifecycle -> ["delay <delta>"] then "event <data>"
  .rx        -> ["delay <delta>"] then "rx <hex>"

delta    = max(0, entry.offsetMs - lastOffsetMs), emitted only when > 0
offsetMs = max(0, Int((Date().timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate - sessionStartTimestamp) * 1000))
           and 0 while no session has started
hex      = bytes.map { String(format: "%02x", $0) }.joined(separator: " ")
output   = lines.joined(separator: "\n") + "\n"

That output is valid input for ReplayScript.parse(text:), so a field capture replays deterministically against the same kernels that produced it.

Desync annotations are deduplicated by content, not by time:

EBoardDiagnosticDeduplication.desyncKey(positionFEN:occupancyHex:resolutions:)
    = "\(positionFEN)|\(occupancyHex)|"
      + resolutions.map { $0.moves.joined(separator: ",") }.joined(separator: ";")

The shell kernel logs squareoff desync: fen=<fen> choices=<n> board=<hex> and annotates desync fen=<fen> choices=<n> only when this key differs from context.desyncDedupKey, so a board parked in one mismatched state fills the ring with one entry rather than five hundred.

Encoding a 500-entry capture and atomically replacing its file are delegated to EBoardDiagnosticPersistenceCoordinator, a @MainActor facade over a private actor:

let persistence = EBoardDiagnosticPersistenceCoordinator()   // 250 ms debounce

capture.annotate("uci e2e4")
persistence.schedule(capture, immediate: false) { json in
    blobStore.saveJSON(json, forKey: EBoardDiagnosticCapture.blobKey)
    return true            // false = writer failed; the snapshot is not marked durable
}

// Lifecycle and take-back boundaries skip the delay but still encode off-main.
persistence.schedule(capture, immediate: true, writer: writer)
persistence.cancelPending()      // session shutting down

schedule bumps a monotonic revision &+= 1; immediate: true uses delay 0 rather than the 250 ms default. The worker persists only when revision == newestRevision, the capture differs from the last persisted value, JSONEncoder succeeds, and the writer returns true.

docs.title: Board marks
docs.text:
BoardMarkDocument is the shared arrow/circle document, bounded so a corrupt or hostile blob cannot blow up either platform:

Constant Value currentVersion 1 maximumEncodedBytes 1 * 1_024 * 1_024 maximumPositions 4_096 maximumMarksPerPosition 128 maximumTotalMarks 16_384 maximumPositionKeyBytes 512

Validation requires version == 1, a non-empty position key within the byte limit, per-position id uniqueness, both indices in 0..<64, and the geometry invariant: an .arrow needs fromIndex != toIndex, a .circle needs fromIndex == toIndex.

// Editing path: refuse anything this build cannot safely display.
guard let doc = BoardMarkDocument.decodeStrict(rawJSON) else { /* show nothing */ }

// Backup path: never normalize a future document into an empty drawing.
let preserved = BoardMarkDocument.decodePreserving(rawJSON)
preserved.isRecognized           // false when the source was retained verbatim
preserved.encoded()              // the exact original bytes in that case

encoded() returns the preserved source when unrecognized, "" when every position list is empty (the historical blank sentinel), and otherwise JSON with [.sortedKeys, .withoutEscapingSlashes] after dropping empty position arrays. That last property is what makes a recognized document usable as digest input. BoardMark's decoder treats a missing kind as .arrow for Apple v1 compatibility, while an unknown explicit kind still throws — which is exactly what routes it to the byte-preserving path.

docs.title: Presentation strings
docs.text:
BoardSyncPresentation is nonisolated and imports no SwiftUI: semantic state and user-facing copy live here once, and each platform maps state to its own colors and symbols.

Call Result SummaryState(hasSnapshot: false, mismatchCount: _) .noSnapshot → "No board snapshot yet" SummaryState(hasSnapshot: true, mismatchCount: 0) .inSync → "In sync" SummaryState(hasSnapshot: true, mismatchCount: 3) .outOfSync(count: 3) → "3 squares out of sync" syncStripMessage(hasPendingResolutions: true, mismatchCount: _) "Choose how to apply the board's move" syncStripMessage(hasPendingResolutions: false, mismatchCount: 1) "1 square out of sync — tap to fix" otbResult(for: .checkmate, activeColor: .white) "Black wins by checkmate" (the winner is the non-active color) otbResult(for: .stalemate, activeColor: _) "Draw by stalemate" otbResult(for: .insufficientMaterial, activeColor: _) "Draw — insufficient material" otbResult(for: .repetition, activeColor: _) "Draw by threefold repetition" otbResult(for: .playing, activeColor: _) nil (game is live; .check is also nil)

The same file extends BoardCorrectionPlanner.Correction with instruction — "Move the piece on <from> to <square> (<piece.descriptiveName>)", "Place the <piece.descriptiveName> on <square>", or "Remove the piece on <square>" — and [Correction] with placeSquares / removeSquares for lighting the board.

docs.title: Headless surface
docs.text:
Everything in the decision path runs in a command-line tool today. A capture, its brand, and a starting position are enough to reproduce a field bug exactly:

import ChessCore
import FianchettoKit

let core = EBoardSessionCore()
var position = Position.initial()

func gameView() -> EBoardSessionCore.GameView {
    EBoardSessionCore.GameView(
        position: position,
        currentNodeUCI: nil,
        ancestorPositions: ancestors,          // index 0 = 1 ply back
        legalCastlingRookHomes: rookHomes
    )
}

// Feed one decoded board event and run the deferred search inline.
var effects = core.handle(
    event: .occupancySnapshot(occupancy),
    game: gameView(),
    orientationFlipped: false
)

for effect in effects {
    guard case .resolveBoardDiff(let request) = effect else { continue }
    let resolutions = BoardDiffResolver.resolve(
        from: request.position,
        targetOccupancy: request.targetOccupancy,
        maxDepth: 3,
        limit: 8
    )
    effects += core.completeBoardDiffResolution(resolutions, for: request, game: gameView())
}

// Inspect the mismatch without applying anything.
core.occupancyMismatches(game: gameView())   // ["d4", "e5"]
core.corrections(game: gameView()).map(\.instruction)

EBoardPositionTransition.connectingMove(from:to:) closes the loop in the other direction for write-back: it brute-forces MoveGenerator.legalMoves(for:), applies each candidate with MoveGenerator.applyMoveUnchecked into a copy, and returns the first whose resulting Position equals the target — comparing Position values rather than building a FEN string per candidate.

if let move = EBoardPositionTransition.connectingMove(from: previous, to: current) {
    for effect in core.present(move: move, positionBefore: previous) { /* apply */ }
}

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
No fianchetto-cli subcommand covers the e-board layer yet. The natural downstream step is already there: a game recorded over the board exports as PGN and annotates through the engine path — available from the command line as fianchetto-cli annotate.

Three e-board subcommands are proposed, each following the suite's JSON-lines contract (one request object per stdin line, one response per stdout line in request order, diagnostics on stderr, and {"id": …, "error": …} for a bad line):

Proposed Stdin Stdout eboard-replay {"id":…,"brand":"squareOffPro","startFEN":…,"replay":"<.replay text>"} one line per decided event: {"id":…,"effects":[…],"fen":…} eboard-diff {"id":…,"fen":…,"occupancy":"<64 chars of 0/1>","maxDepth":3,"limit":8} {"id":…,"resolutions":[{"moves":["e2e4"],"depth":1}],"mismatches":["e2","e4"]} eboard-catalog none (argument-only) one line per BoardCatalogKey: key, display name, GATT spec fields, scansByName

eboard-diff is the pure kernel call and needs no transport at all; eboard-replay needs only the capture text, since asReplayText() already encodes the frames and their relative timing.

docs.title: Endgame mining and the endgame trainer
docs.text:
Two connected subsystems. The trainer generates fresh legal FENs for eight curated archetypes and bounds the tablebase probe/regeneration loop. The mining pipeline turns the user's own games into drill positions and caches them as immutable, content-addressed, sync-safe generations.

Everything here is pure logic: value types — apart from the two caller-confined scratch classes, EndgameMiningV2OrderingSpool and EndgameMiningV2ScratchLease — plus (String) -> String? load closures, injected FileManager, no actor isolation and no storage backend.

Layer Types What it decides Extraction PersonalEndgameExtractor, PersonalEndgameSourceAnalysis which position in a game is the endgame decision point Witnesses EndgameMiningManifest, EndgameMiningGenerationCommit that a source was examined, and that a generation is complete V1 storage EndgameMiningShard, EndgameMiningGenerationRecord, EndgameMiningStorageHead how a generation is partitioned into bounded rows V1 reconciliation EndgameMiningGenerationResolver, EndgameMiningReclamationPolicy which visible head wins, and what may be deleted V2 storage EndgameMiningV2SourceResult, EndgameMiningV2ResultShard, EndgameMiningV2IndexPage generation-neutral results in a radix-16 trie V2 writing EndgameMiningV2StorageBuilder, EndgameMiningV2OrderingSpool, EndgameMiningV2ScratchLease streaming construction under bounded memory, disk and ownership Trainer EndgamePuzzle, EndgameProbeGuard, EndgameFeedback which drill to show, when to regenerate, what counts as a miss

docs.title: Extraction: what counts as a personal endgame
docs.text:
PersonalEndgameExtractor walks a game's main line and returns at most one position — the first point where the user was to move and the board had dropped into tablebase range while still holding material worth drilling. One position per game keeps the list varied instead of yielding twenty near-duplicates from a single long endgame.

for ply i in 0 ..< mainLine.count:
    position   = mainLine[i].positionBefore        # the decision point
    pieceCount = non-empty squares of position
    require 4 <= pieceCount <= 7                   # else continue
    require mover(ply: i, startIsWhite:) == userColor
    emit one PersonalEndgamePosition and stop

7 is Lichess tablebase coverage; 4 is the least material that is still a drill. The emitted position carries fen (positionBefore.stockfishSafeFEN), gameInfo ("<white> vs <black>"), moveNumber (the position's fullmoveNumber), pieceCount, userColor, and a category material summary read off the board — "K+R vs K+P", "K+Q vs K+R".

PersonalEndgamePosition.id is its fen, so rebuilding the projection from an immutable generation does not hand every row a new identity and make a list diff treat unchanged positions as new. PersonalEndgamePositionData is the Codable form: it flattens userColor to userColorRaw ("white" / "black") so one plain-JSON shape is shared by iOS and Android, and decodes leniently (fen "", gameInfo "", moveNumber 1, pieceCount 4, userColorRaw "white", category "").

currentRevision is 4, and it is one of the three fields of the source key. Bumping it when eligibility or emitted semantics change is what stops an old negative result from suppressing a newer extractor: revision 5 produces different sources, so every game is reconsidered.

docs.title: Source identity without replay
docs.text:
A cache needs a key that is cheap to compute. Constructing every intermediate position merely to discover whether a result is reusable would defeat the purpose, so sourceDigest(input:) hashes the lexical PGN semantics. Tokenization drops comments, variations, NAGs, move numbers and results, so a plain copy and the app's annotated rewrite of the same game hash identically.

PortableSHA256; every field length-prefixed
  (8-byte big-endian UTF-8 length, then the bytes)

domain   "personal-endgame-source:v4"
then     input.white
         input.black
         input.username
         canonicalStartingPositionIdentity(input.startingPositionFEN)
then     decimal count of main-line moves
then     each canonicalized SAN, in order

canonicalStartingPositionIdentity(fen):
    trimmed.isEmpty -> Position.initial().fen
    otherwise       -> Position(fen: trimmed)?.fen ?? trimmed

canonicalLexicalSAN(san):
    remove '+', '#', '!', '?'; trim whitespace
    "0-0" -> "O-O",  "0-0-0" -> "O-O-O"

The normalization is deliberately conservative: if two unusual SAN spellings are not provably equivalent lexically they become separate sources and are replayed, rather than risking an incorrect cache hit. An invalid starting FEN stays byte-identifiable for repair diagnostics.

Note

This digest is an admission witness, not a completion witness. A match at the same extractor revision may reuse a previously validated result; a miss must still complete a diagnostic-free semantic replay before it can publish either positions or noPositions.

docs.title: Completion versus rejection
docs.text:
analyze(stableGameID:from:) validates and replays one exact source once and returns .completed or .rejected. Only .completed carries a PersonalEndgameCompletedExtraction, whose initializer is fileprivate — nothing outside the extractor can mint one, so a permissive empty legacy result cannot retire a source as complete.

Rejection Cause insufficientInput white, black, username or move text is blank invalidStableGameID empty, or not equal to GameIdentity.normalizedIdentifier of its own NFC-precomposed form unresolvedUserColor the saved account name matches neither player invalidMainLine(diagnostic) ChessCore reported a replay diagnostic insufficientMainLine the record parsed but yielded no playable move

PersonalEndgameMainLineDiagnostic carries bounded context — invalidFEN(preview:), unparseableMove(san:plyIndex:), tagsOnlyRecord, moveTreeNodeLimitExceeded(maximumNodes:), other. Previews are truncated before they enter the value: the first 96 unicode scalars, whitespace runs collapsed to single spaces, "…" appended when anything was dropped. Surfacing an error can therefore never echo a whole PGN. The diagnostic itself is a plain value; every case renders a distinct user-facing message through the rejection's errorDescription (PersonalEndgameExtractionCompletionError is the LocalizedError), and unparseableMove reports a 1-based "ply \(max(0, plyIndex) + 1)".

Warning

A rejection is retry-eligible and must never become a durable noPositions manifest. noPositions means "this exact source was examined and intentionally produced nothing"; a rejection means "this source could not be examined".

let input = TacticsInput(
    white: game.white,
    black: game.black,
    moveText: game.moveText,
    tagsJSON: game.tagsJSON,
    annotationEvalsJSON: "",
    username: account
)

switch PersonalEndgameExtractor.analyze(stableGameID: game.stableID, from: input) {
case .completed(let extraction):
    let admission = try EndgameMiningStorageAdmission(
        completedExtraction: extraction,
        whitePlayerName: input.white,
        blackPlayerName: input.black
    )
    stage(try admission.manifest(generation: 1, completedExtraction: extraction))

case .rejected(let error):
    report(error.errorDescription)      // retry-eligible; record nothing durable
}

EndgameMiningStorageAdmission bounds display metadata before it can enter coverage: stableGameID at 512 UTF-8 bytes, white + black player names at 384 UTF-8 bytes combined, else sourceNotStorable. Without that gate one game with a pathological label could make every full-library generation fail forever at the shard writer. Skipped sources should be counted and reconsidered on each rescan; authored game data is never truncated. manifest(...) re-checks that the extraction's source equals the admitted one (commitMismatch) and that the record is shard-storable.

docs.title: Witnesses: manifests, outcomes, coverage
docs.text:
EndgameMiningManifest is one immutable per-source V1 result. Its Source is the triple (stableGameID, sourceDigest, extractorRevision) — the full triple is the key, so one game can be mined for several account identities without collision. sourceDigest must be canonical lowercase SHA-256 (64 hex) and extractorRevision must be positive.

Outcome cardinality — enforced on construction AND on decode:
    (.noPositions, 0 positions)   ok
    (.positions,   1 position)    ok
    anything else                 throw .invalidOutcome

Position validity:
    FEN parses; moveNumber > 0; userColorRaw ∈ {"white","black"};
    actual board piece count ∈ 4...7 and == the declared pieceCount

manifestDigest = H("endgame-mining-manifest:v1", schemaVersion, generation,
                   source triple, outcome.kind, position count,
                   each position's six fields)

The single-position invariant freezes today's extractor into storage so a malformed record cannot turn one bounded shard into an unbounded payload; a multi-position policy must bump both revision and schema.

Coverage and the commit are built in constant memory from a canonically ordered stream, so no library-sized array is ever materialized.

V1 source order (EndgameMiningSourceOrder.precedes):
    stableGameID, then sourceDigest, then extractorRevision

Coverage.Builder: seed "endgame-mining-coverage:v1"; per source append the three
    fields length-prefixed (duplicate -> .duplicateSource,
    out of order -> .sourceOutOfOrder); finish by hashing the decimal count.

Commit Builder: seed "endgame-mining-set:v1"; per manifest append its
    manifestDigest; finish by hashing the decimal count, then require
    rebuiltCoverage == expectedCoverage else .coverageMismatch.

generationDigest = H("endgame-mining-generation:v1", schemaVersion, generation,
                     coverage.sourceCount, coverage.sourceSetDigest,
                     manifestSetDigest)

Because finish() refuses a partial source set, a cancelled prefix can leave unreachable immutable shards but can never become a visible generation. EndgameMiningHead binds to generationDigest; legacyGeneration = 0 names the historical flat cache, and decode admits only (0, nil) or (>= 1, canonical SHA-256).

docs.title: V1 storage layout
docs.text:
Every sync-visible row is bounded and content-addressed, so the encoded payload stays independent of library size.

Object Bound Storage key manifest (inside a shard) 8 KiB — EndgameMiningShard 96 manifests, 900 KiB personalEndgames/shard/v1/<shardDigest> EndgameMiningGenerationRecord 10 922 shards, 768 KiB personalEndgames/generation/v1/<recordDigest> EndgameMiningStorageHead 4 KiB personalEndgames/head/v1 EndgameMiningProjectionReceipt 8 KiB personalEndgames/projectionReceipt/v1 
maximumSourceCount = 10_922 * 96 = 1_048_512

expectedShardCount(sourceCount):
    0                        when sourceCount == 0
    ((sourceCount - 1) / 96) + 1   otherwise

expectedManifestCount(inShardAt: i):
    96                                    for every non-final shard
    sourceCount % 96, or 96 when that remainder is 0, for the last

Since every non-final shard holds exactly 96 manifests, the source count in the commit determines the entire partition — the layout is unique and a repartitioned copy is rejected with invalidCanonicalPartition. The record also binds its parent (EndgameMiningGenerationIdentity, .legacy = (0, nil, nil)) and requires commit.generation == parent.generation + 1. EndgameMiningStorageNamespace marks all of this as infrastructure: keys under personalEndgames/ (or the reserved legacy personalEndgames_) are sync and crash-recovery machinery, so semantic library backups carry only the flat projection.

EndgameMiningGenerationStorageBuilder writes a generation in constant source memory: feed manifests in canonical order, persist each shard append(_:) returns as it crosses a 96-manifest boundary, then publish Completion(finalShard, commit, generationRecord, storageHead) in exactly that order. Every fallible mutation is staged in value copies, so a rejected append leaves the builder reusable and cannot silently drop a full shard.

docs.title: The canonical-JSON contract
docs.text:
EndgameMiningStorageCodec (and its V2 twin) is the only supported entry point, because a bare JSONDecoder enforces neither half of the contract:

encode: JSONEncoder with [.sortedKeys, .withoutEscapingSlashes]
        reject when data.count > maximumBytes  ->  .payloadTooLarge(limit:)

decode: reject empty, or source.utf8.count > maximumBytes — BEFORE decoding, so
        nested arrays cannot be allocated first
        decode, re-encode, require byte-for-byte equality
        otherwise -> .nonCanonicalJSON

The byte-exact re-encode rejects unknown fields, alternate key order, insignificant whitespace and noncanonical escaping. It is also why the same bytes compare equal across platforms.

docs.title: V1 reconciliation
docs.text:
EndgameMiningGenerationResolver.resolve(...) compares all visible head copies against a freshly recomputed source universe and returns .promote or .retainCurrent(reason).

if headJSONCandidates.count > 4_096  ->  .retainCurrent(.candidateLimitExceeded)

decode candidates, drop legacy heads
append the current receipt's head (a receipt is itself a durable head witness, so
    a missing or hidden physical head row cannot lose it)
sort DESCENDING by (generation, generationDigest, generationRecordDigest);
    skip exact repeats

per candidate:
    skip when precedes(candidate, currentHead)            # monotonic floor
    skip when candidate == currentHead and its record coverage ==
         expectedCoverage and the flat cache matches the receipt
    require the record loads, head.accepts(record),
            record.commit.coverage == expectedCoverage
    fully revalidate every shard  ->  .promote

else .retainCurrent(currentReceipt == nil ? .noCompleteGeneration
                                          : .currentGenerationPreferred)

Two rules carry the weight. The receipt is an unconditional monotonic floor: temporary object loss or a changed live source universe may make its projection unusable, but neither authorizes a passive rollback to an older sync-visible generation. And parent identity is audit metadata, not an admission gate — requiring ancestry would permanently fork replicas that advanced opposite sides of a concurrent head race, so deterministic digest tie-breaking is what makes them converge.

EndgameMiningValidatedGeneration (mintable only by the resolver) re-derives the commit while streaming, checking each shard's content address, generation and expected manifest count, and finally requiring builder.finish() == record.commit.

docs.title: V2: generation-neutral results in a radix-16 trie
docs.text:
V1 embeds the scan generation in every manifest digest, so every full scan rewrites every row. V2 removes the generation from result identity, which makes an unchanged source referencable by every later generation.

sourceKeyDigest = H("endgame-mining-source-key:v2", source triple)
resultDigest    = H("endgame-mining-result:v2", schemaVersion, source triple,
                    outcome.kind, each position's six fields, position count)

V2 order: sourceKeyDigest first; on a hash collision fall back to the V1 tuple
          (stableGameID, sourceDigest, extractorRevision)

EndgameMiningV2SourceResult reuses the V1 manifest kernel for semantic validation (constructed at firstManifestGeneration) without keeping that generation in the value or either hash. Results live in a content-addressed trie keyed by hex nibbles of sourceKeyDigest:

leaf: buffer results while count <= 96
97th: split into a radix-16 index page keyed by the nibble at
      depth = prefix.utf8.count, then reapply the rule recursively
depth: a 64-character prefix exhausts the hash -> .hashPrefixExhausted

Result shard: every result's sourceKeyDigest starts with the shard prefix;
    results strictly V2-ordered; no duplicate source.
Index page:   children strictly ascending by nibble; unique child digests;
    <= 16 children; prefix shorter than 64; summed sourceCount > 96, so a page
    can never stand in for a leaf.
Node reference: sourceCount > 0; resultShard <= 96; indexPage > 96.

Only one child per level is ever active, which bounds writer memory at 96 buffered results plus at most 16 child references per level.

Object Bound Storage key EndgameMiningV2SourceResult 8 KiB — (inside a shard or a spool frame) EndgameMiningV2ResultShard 96 results, 900 KiB personalEndgames/result/v2/<shardDigest> EndgameMiningV2IndexPage 16 children, 16 KiB personalEndgames/index/v2/<pageDigest> EndgameMiningV2GenerationRecord 1 048 512 sources, 16 KiB personalEndgames/generation/v2/<recordDigest> EndgameMiningV2StorageHead 4 KiB personalEndgames/head/v2 EndgameMiningV2ProjectionReceipt 8 KiB personalEndgames/projectionReceipt/v2

The generation record is a compact selection record — coverage proof (endgame-mining-coverage:v2), result-set proof (endgame-mining-result-set:v2), and the root reference. It requires generation == parent.generation + 1, coverage.sourceCount == resultSet.resultCount, and either (0 sources, nil root) or (>= 1 sources, root.sourceCount == coverage.sourceCount). hasEquivalentSourceResults(to:) is the publisher's no-op predicate — coverage, result set and root only, ignoring generation and parent.

docs.title: Writing a V2 generation
docs.text:
EndgameMiningV2StorageBuilder.append(_:) is transactional: coverage, result-set and trie state are staged in copies before commit, and it rejects duplicateSource, invalidCanonicalOrder and tooManySources(limit: 1_048_512). Artifacts stream out dependency-first as subtrees complete, so each can be persisted immediately; finish() returns the remaining artifacts ending with the root, plus the generation record and head.

Results must arrive in V2 order. A platform whose enumeration is not already in hash order uses EndgameMiningV2OrderingSpool, a caller-scoped disk-backed radix sort that creates and exclusively owns a previously nonexistent directory and removes it after every successful or failed build.

Frame layout (68 bytes of overhead per record):
    4-byte big-endian JSON length | 64-byte source key | canonical JSON

drain(file, expectedCount, prefix, depth):
    expectedCount <= 96:
        read every frame; require the decoded sourceKeyDigest to equal the frame
        header and to start with `prefix`; sort in memory by
        EndgameMiningV2SourceOrder; feed the trie builder
    otherwise:
        require depth < 64
        partition into up to 16 child files by the nibble at `depth`
        a bucket > 96 whose source keys are all identical throws
            .tooManyEquivalentSourceKeys(limit: 96) rather than copying the same
            input through all 64 radix levels
        recurse over "0123456789abcdef" in order
Constant Value maximumDecodedBatchResultCount 96 maximumInMemoryResultCount 192 (a batch plus the writer's retained leaf) maximumSimultaneouslyOpenFileHandles 17 (one reader, sixteen writers) maximumSimultaneouslyResidentScratchFiles 15 · 64 + 17 = 977 maximumSpoolBytes 1 048 512 · (8 192 + 68) = 8 660 709 120 maximumWorkingBytes twice that — a partition holds its source and its copy minimumFreeCapacityReserveBytes 512 MiB workingDirectoryNamePrefix fianchetto-endgame-mining-v2-spool-

Before each write the spool accumulates bytes and re-probes free capacity every 16 MiB, requiring available >= 512 MiB + 16 MiB or throwing insufficientScratchCapacity(minimumAvailableBytes:) — rendered as MiB by ceiling division on 1 048 576. The reserve leaves room for app recovery, database journals and an actionable error instead of consuming the volume to zero. States run accepting -> sealed -> draining -> finished | failed; any failure closes and removes the whole directory, and a cleanup failure supersedes the operation error so a retained spool is never mistaken for a clean one. reclaimStaleWorkingDirectories(in:olderThan:...) sweeps abandoned directories at startup (defaults: 256 scanned entries, 8 removals).

let lease = try EndgameMiningV2ScratchLease.acquire(in: scratchParent)
defer { try? lease.release() }

let spool = try EndgameMiningV2OrderingSpool(
    directory: EndgameMiningV2OrderingSpool.workingDirectoryURL(in: scratchParent)
)

for extraction in completedExtractions {
    try spool.append(EndgameMiningV2SourceResult(completedExtraction: extraction))
    try lease.checkpoint()          // fails closed if this owner was displaced
}

let completion = try spool.build(
    generation: nextGeneration,
    parent: parentIdentity
) { artifact in
    try store.write(artifact.storageKey, artifact.canonicalJSON())
}

// Publish only after every immutable node is durable.
try store.write(completion.generationRecord.storageKey,
                EndgameMiningV2StorageCodec.encodeCanonical(completion.generationRecord))
try store.write(EndgameMiningV2StorageHead.storageKey,
                EndgameMiningV2StorageCodec.encodeCanonical(completion.storageHead))

Warning

The spool is intentionally not Sendable and performs synchronous file I/O. Create, append and build it on one caller-owned worker; never drive it from several actors or threads.

docs.title: Scratch ownership
docs.text:
A spool can legitimately reach several gigabytes, so age-only cleanup is not enough: repeated force-termination can leave several fresh spools before any becomes reclaimable. EndgameMiningV2ScratchLease permits one owner per app-private parent directory.

acquire: up to 4 attempts at exclusive creation of
         "fianchetto-endgame-mining-v2-lease"

if it exists, observe (owner.json bytes, directory mtime, heartbeat):
    the owner is fresh — takeover forbidden — when the reference time is within
    5 minutes OR lies in the future (a clock rollback must never license two
    owners)

otherwise: same-volume rename to
           "fianchetto-endgame-mining-v2-retired-lease-<UUID>", re-observe, and
           require byte-identical metadata (else restore it and report
           .leaseBusy); then re-create the lease and delete the retired copy

checkpoint(): re-read the token every call — mismatch -> .leaseLost;
              rewrite the heartbeat at most every 5 seconds

Predecessor cleanup is bounded to 512 scanned parent entries, 64 spool directories and 16 retired leases; exceeding any of them throws cleanupLimitExceeded instead of scanning an unbounded directory.

docs.title: Reading, merging and projecting
docs.text:
EndgameMiningV2ValidatedGeneration (public init, throwing headMismatch unless head.accepts(record)) rebuilds the coverage and result-set proofs while descending, checking each node's prefix, digest and sourceCount against its reference (recordMismatch otherwise) and bounding the walk:

maximumNodeCount = maximumSourceCount + 64 * (maximumSourceCount / 97 + 1)
                 = 1_048_512 + 64 * 10_810
                 = 1_740_352 visited nodes before .tooManyNodes

forEachReusableResult(currentSources:loadObjectJSON:_:) is the single-pass merge kernel publishers use instead of a library-sized dictionary. It validates currentSources through a V2 coverage builder (rejecting an out-of-order or duplicated universe up front), traverses both streams once in V2 order, invokes the callback on each exact source match, and returns a [Bool] reuse bitmap — every unset entry must be re-extracted. Callbacks can run before a later corrupt dependency is discovered, so callers must stage writes and commit only after the method returns.

De-duplication reproduces V1 output byte-for-byte regardless of trie layout:

V1: walk manifests in canonical source order, keep the FIRST occurrence of a FEN
V2: traverse in hash order; for a duplicate FEN keep the winner with the MINIMUM
    source under EndgameMiningSourceOrder, then sort survivors by that same order

The receipt distinguishes a valid current cache from a partially written one: it requires a non-legacy head and unique FENs, and hashes the head identity, then each position's six fields, then the count (endgame-mining-projection:v1 / :v2).

switch EndgameMiningV2GenerationResolver.resolveProjection(
    currentReceipt: receipt,
    currentProjectionMatchesReceipt: receipt?.accepts(currentPositions) ?? false,
    expectedCoverage: expectedCoverage,
    headJSONCandidates: perReplicaHeadJSON,
    loadGenerationRecordJSON: { store.string(forKey: $0) },
    loadObjectJSON: { store.string(forKey: $0) }
) {
case .promote(let projection):
    // Atomically replace the flat cache and its receipt — never union them.
    try store.replaceMinedEndgames(projection.positions,
                                   receipt: projection.receipt)
case .retainCurrent(let reason):
    log("kept the current projection: \(reason)")
}

resolve and resolveProjection share one ranking kernel — (generation, generationRecordDigest) descending, the same 4 096-candidate limit, the same receipt-as-floor rule — and evaluate runs at most once per unique viable head, so the winning trie is walked exactly once whether the caller wanted strict validation or a materialized projection. Missing or corrupt higher dependencies never hide a lower complete candidate.

docs.title: Retention
docs.text:
Every full V1 scan creates a new generation, because generation identity is part of the manifest proof. EndgameMiningReclamationPolicy.plan(...) keeps that from growing without bound.

retain: "personalEndgames/head/v1", plus for each distinct non-legacy visible
        head (INCLUDING the current receipt's) its generation-record key and
        every shard key that record names

defer the whole pass (isDeferred) when candidates exceed 4_096, or an active
        record is missing / undecodable / not accepted by its head — a
        not-yet-arrived directory is the only safe way to discover its shards

reclaim only when ALL hold:
        the key starts with "personalEndgames/shard/v1/"
                         or "personalEndgames/generation/v1/"
        it is unretained
        now - lastModified >= 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1_000 ms  (2_592_000_000)

The 30-day floor covers long offline and sync intervals. Platforms may use a longer interval, never a shorter one.

docs.title: Storage epochs
docs.text:
Occasionally a physical namespace must be retired — a container reset — without changing any semantic V2 object. Epochs give identical bytes a permanently distinct address. EndgameMiningV2StorageEpochIdentity is (sequence, descriptorDigest), valid only as (0, nil) (the shipped unscoped keys) or (>= 1, canonical SHA-256). The descriptor (sequence = parent.sequence + 1, 8 KiB, personalEndgames/storageEpoch/v1/<digest>) binds a transition nonce and the exact replica roster under endgame-mining-v2-storage-epoch:v1.

epoch 0: exact identity mapping of the logical key

epoch n: "personalEndgames/v2e/" + descriptorDigest + "/" + kind + "." + digest
         kind ∈ { "r" result shard, "i" index page, "g" generation record }

reverse: exactly 4 slash-separated components; [0] == "personalEndgames",
         [1] == "v2e", [2] == the epoch digest, canonical SHA-256 after the '.'

loadLogicalJSON(for:epoch:loadPhysicalJSON:) is shaped to be handed straight to the graph walks. EndgameMiningV2EpochStorageHead (prefix personalEndgames/head/v2e/ plus a validated EndgameMiningReplicaID — up to 128 bytes of [0-9A-Za-z._-]) and EndgameMiningV2EpochProjectionReceipt both reject a legacy epoch or legacy inner value and hash the canonical inner JSON (endgame-mining-v2-epoch-head:v1, endgame-mining-v2-epoch-projection:v1), so identical inner heads in different epochs are never interchangeable authority.

docs.title: The trainer runtime
docs.text:
EndgamePuzzle pairs an archetype with a training tip. Its FEN is regenerated on every attempt, so the spaced-repetition key is deliberately FEN-independent:

public var masteryKey: String { "\(archetype.rawValue):\(description)" }

The static catalogue holds 12 drills — two K+Q vs K, two K+R vs K, one K+2B vs K, one K+B+N vs K, three K+P vs K, one Lucena, one Philidor, one K+Q vs K+P. Mastery counts persist through BlunderMasteryStore (see Stores).

EndgameProbeGuard bounds the "regenerate when the tablebase says drawn" loop and rejects stale in-flight probes:

beginSetup(isRegen:)  currentToken &+= 1; regenAttempts = 0 unless isRegen
isStale(token:)       nil -> false (unowned mid-puzzle re-probes are fresh);
                      otherwise token != currentToken
decideOnDraw()        regenAttempts < maxRegenAttempts (default 3)
                          -> increment and return .regen
                      otherwise -> .exhausted, permanently, for this puzzle

var probeGuard = EndgameProbeGuard()          // maxRegenAttempts: 3
var fen = puzzle.archetype.randomFEN()
let token = probeGuard.beginSetup()

let probe = try await TablebaseService.shared.probe(fen: fen)
guard !probeGuard.isStale(token: token) else { return }   // a newer setup won

if probe.category == .draw {
    switch probeGuard.decideOnDraw() {
    case .regen:
        fen = puzzle.archetype.randomFEN()
        _ = probeGuard.beginSetup(isRegen: true)   // keeps the attempt count
    case .exhausted:
        present(fen)                               // stop looping
    }
}

EndgameFeedback is the answer verdict: correct(dtm:), closeEnough(dtm:best:), wrong(expected:), tablebaseUnavailable, engineUnavailable, done.

Warning

engineUnavailable means the Stockfish fallback produced no completed score. It is not a chess miss and must not increment attempts or mastery — otherwise a flaky engine silently resets the user's streak.

EndgameProbeGuard owns the trainer's own probe tokens; RunGeneration is the separate general-purpose restartable-work token the long-running schedulers use (Maia backfill, the Android mining run lifecycle). begin() and invalidate() both do current &+= 1 (invalidate revokes without granting), and owns(_:) is exact equality. Capture a token, then publish or clear shared state only while owns(_:) holds: cancellation cannot synchronously stop code already inside a non-cancellable framework call, so a predecessor may reach its cleanup after its replacement has started.

docs.title: Position generation
docs.text:
EndgameArchetype.randomFEN() retries attemptGenerate() up to 200 times, then returns the per-case fallbackFEN (kqVsK → "8/8/8/4k3/8/3Q4/3K4/8 w - - 0 1", philidor → "8/8/4k3/8/4K3/r7/4P3/3R4 b - - 0 1"). Each random-square primitive retries 50 times before returning to the outer loop. Lucena and Philidor are hard-coded template families (5 and 4 templates), varying the file while preserving the technique.

Kings are never adjacent (Chebyshev distance <= 1 is forbidden).
A piece adjacent to the enemy king is admitted only when the friendly king
    also defends it.

K+Q vs K, K+R vs K  black king on files/ranks 2...5; white king at Chebyshev
                    distance 2...4
K+2B vs K, K+B+N    black king on files/ranks drawn from {1, 2, 5, 6};
                    white king at distance 2...5
K+P vs K            pawn on 0-indexed rank 2...5; white king within distance
                    1...2 of the square in front of the pawn and never on
                    rank 0; black king at distance 2...4 from the pawn, not
                    adjacent to the white king, not on a pawn-attacked square
K+Q vs K+P          black pawn on 0-indexed rank 1...2, white to move

Finalization is where "legal" becomes "drillable":

finalize(pos):
    reject when the side NOT to move is in check
        (the previous move would have been illegal)
    reject when the side to move has no legal move
        (mate or stalemate is not a drill)
    emit pos.stockfishSafeFEN

That last line matters: Position() defaults castling rights to all-true and a random endgame layout has no kings or rooks on their home squares. stockfishSafeFEN zeros castling and en-passant state inconsistent with the board, which is what stops these FENs from crashing Stockfish's strict parser downstream.

CustomEndgameConfig covers material outside the curated catalogue. PieceCounts clamps queens, rooks, bishops and knights to 0...maxPerPieceType (4) and pawns to 0...8; totalPieces = 2 + white.totalNonKing + black.totalNonKing, and isValid is totalPieces <= 32. Generation places the black king centrally, then the non-adjacent white king, then non-pawn pieces under the en-prise/defended rule, then pawns on 0-indexed ranks 1...6 with white pawns forbidden from attacking the black king. randomFEN() returns nil after 200 failed attempts; fallbackFEN is "8/8/8/4k3/8/4K3/8/8 w - - 0 1".

Note

Positions above 7 pieces fall outside Lichess tablebase coverage, so the trainer skips win verification for them. See Network clients for TablebaseService.

docs.title: Using it from the command line
docs.text:
Every seam above is already headless, which is what makes it scriptable without an app. fianchetto-cli today ships annotate, estimate, maia, accuracy, project and track; none of them wrap this pipeline yet. The natural split follows the three proofs:

Proposed subcommand Seam it would expose endgame-mine PersonalEndgameExtractor.analyze + EndgameMiningStorageAdmission + EndgameMiningV2OrderingSpool.build over a PGN corpus, emitting trie artifacts endgame-verify EndgameMiningV2ValidatedGeneration.validate / EndgameMiningGenerationResolver.resolve against a directory of head copies endgame-pack materializeProjection to the flat position cache plus its receipt

Because every digest is PortableSHA256 over length-prefixed UTF-8 and every envelope is byte-exact canonical JSON, golden digest fixtures are the cheapest parity test available: mine a fixed corpus once, record the sourceDigest, resultDigest, shardDigest, recordDigest and projectionDigest values, and assert that the iOS and Android implementations reproduce them byte-for-byte.

docs.title: Engine & Annotation
docs.text: How FianchettoKit turns a game into per-move glyphs, quality labels, accuracy numbers, and an eval chart — and how it does that without ever naming a concrete engine.

docs.title: The four stages
docs.text:
Stage Owner Input → output Collect evals AnnotationDriver.collectEvals(positions:evaluator:onProgress:) [Position] → [AnnotationEval]? Normalize UCI AnnotationKernel.extractEval(fromRankedInfos:bestMoveUCI:) [Int: UCIInfo] rank map → AnnotationEval? Classify per ply AnnotationKernel.computeAnnotations(inputs:evals:startIsWhite:) inputs + evals → [NodeAnnotationResult] Write back AnnotationKernel.applyAnnotations(_:to:game:) results → MoveNode fields

The rule that makes this portable: the pipeline depends on the role of a position evaluator — the PositionEvaluator protocol — never on a concrete engine. Stages 2 and 3 are pure functions over Sendable value types, so they can run on a detached task and the whole classification is testable without a running engine; only stage 4 touches the non-Sendable MoveNode / Game.

docs.title: Choosing an engine
docs.text:
AnnotationEngineKind (String, CaseIterable, Codable, Sendable) is the registry of engines a user may pick to drive annotation: .stockfish → displayName "Stockfish", .reckless → "Reckless".

AnnotationEngineKind.settingsKey            // "annotationEngine"
AnnotationEngineKind.resolve(nil)           // .stockfish
AnnotationEngineKind.resolve("reckless")    // .reckless
AnnotationEngineKind.resolve("maia")        // .stockfish — unknown values fall back

resolve(_:) never fails: nil, an unknown raw value, or a value naming an engine that no longer qualifies all resolve to .stockfish.

Membership is a capability boundary, not a taste: only evaluating search engines — those producing a best move plus a centipawn or mate score per position — belong here. Maia is deliberately absent, because a human-move predictor (policy + WDL) cannot produce the centipawn deltas blunder-grading is built on. Playing against an engine has no such requirement, which is why PlayConfig.Engine is the wider set .maia / .stockfish / .reckless. Its isAvailable currently returns true for every case and exists as the single future home for platform gating.

docs.title: Search budget
docs.text:
The two budget functions take the same persisted "annotation thoroughness" preference string and scale differently, because Stockfish is driven by movetime while Reckless anneals by fixed depth.

annotateMovetime(batch:thoroughness:)      annotateDepth(thoroughness:)
    base = batch ? 500 : 1000  // ms           "fast"     → 10
    "fast"     → base * 6  / 10                "thorough" → 14
    "thorough" → base * 16 / 10                otherwise  → 12   // ply
    otherwise  → base          // incl. nil

Integer arithmetic throughout, so the six movetimes are exact:

thoroughness batch: true batch: false "fast" 300 ms 600 ms nil / anything else 500 ms 1000 ms "thorough" 800 ms 1600 ms

Available from the command line: fianchetto-cli annotate — a request that omits the movetime_ms field falls back to annotateMovetime(batch: true, thoroughness:).

docs.title: AnnotationEval — the neutral per-position DTO
docs.text:
Every engine's output maps onto this one struct before entering the kernel:

public struct AnnotationEval: Sendable {
    public var bestCp: Int              // engine-POV; mate → ±100_000
    public var secondBestCp: Int?       // nil when MultiPV < 2
    public var isMate: Bool
    public var mateIn: Int?             // signed distance, or nil
    public var bestMoveUCI: String      // "" = no move (terminal)
}

Three conventions carry the design. Engine POV: positive is good for the side to move, in every field; White-POV orientation happens later, once, at the display boundary. The ±100 000 mate sentinel: bestCp flattens a forced mate to +100_000 or -100_000 by sign, so every downstream comparison — win probability, consensus gap, glyph thresholds — works on one Int axis with no special-casing. mateIn is carried separately precisely because bestCp destroys the distance; it is the only place the signed N survives (the missed-mate tactics category needs it) and is nil when the engine did not surface it.

The memberwise initializer defaults secondBestCp and mateIn to nil, isMate to false, and bestMoveUCI to "".

docs.title: Collecting evals
docs.text:
public protocol PositionEvaluator: Sendable {
    func evaluate(fen: String) async -> AnnotationEval?
}

Only non-terminal positions reach a conformer — the driver fills terminal positions itself. Returning nil means the engine failed or went silent, and aborts the whole sweep.

Indexing contract for collectEvals(positions:evaluator:onProgress:)

    positions[0]     = the game's start position
    positions[i + 1] = the position AFTER ply i
    result.count     = positions.count      (or the whole call returns nil)

Per position:
    if Task.isCancelled                → return nil
    if terminalEval(for:) is non-nil   → append it, no engine probe
    else if evaluator returns nil      → return nil          (engine gave up)
    if Task.isCancelled                → return nil
    onProgress(i + 1, positions.count)

Cancellation is checked twice per position — before the potentially second-long probe and again after appending — so a cancelled batch stops promptly rather than at the next position boundary.

Warning

onProgress is @Sendable (completed, total) and may run off the caller's actor. A caller updating actor-isolated UI state must marshal explicitly (Task { @MainActor in … }). It defaults to a no-op.

docs.title: Terminal positions
docs.text:
AnnotationKernel.terminalEval(for:) returns nil when MoveGenerator.legalMoves(for:) is non-empty — the caller's signal to probe the engine. Otherwise:

Position bestCp isMate mateIn bestMoveUCI Checkmate (no legal moves, in check) -100_000 true 0 "" Stalemate (no legal moves, not in check) 0 false nil "" Has legal moves — — — returns nil

Checkmate is mate in 0 from the mated side's POV, matching the engine's own score mate 0 line.

docs.title: From raw UCI to a normalized eval
docs.text:
UCI parsing is foundational chess logic, so ChessCore owns it. FianchettoKit keeps two compatibility aliases so every call site — and the Android port — compiles unchanged:

public typealias UCIInfoLine   = ChessCore.UCIInfo
public typealias UCIInfoParser = ChessCore.UCIOutputParser

The former FianchettoKit kernel copies were collapsed onto ChessCore's after the FianchettoKit parser's improvements (nps parsing, no mandatory pv token, bestmove (none) handling, bestInfoByRank) were folded into ChessCore. ChessCore.UCIInfo is a strict superset of the old line type — it keeps depth, multipv, scoreCp, mateIn, nps, pv, bestMoveUCI, centipawns, winProbability, displayText, whitePovCentipawns, and the whitePovCp / whitePovMate statics, and adds the .score enum view and .multiPV.

extractEval(fromRankedInfos:bestMoveUCI:) resolves a [Int: UCIInfo] rank map (as produced by UCIOutputParser.bestInfoByRank) into an AnnotationEval:

rank 1 missing, or carries no score → return nil   (evaluation unavailable)
rank 1 .mate(m)  → isMate = true,  mateIn = m,   bestCp = ±100_000 by sign of m
rank 1 .cp(cp)   → isMate = false, mateIn = nil, bestCp = cp
rank 2 scored    → secondBestCp = rank2.score.centipawns  (a mate also ±100_000)
rank 2 absent, or present without a score → secondBestCp = nil

Note the asymmetry: the rank-1 guard is what makes an evaluation available, while rank 2 is optional and its absence simply zeroes the MultiPV gap later.

docs.title: EngineScoreAdapter
docs.text:
The sibling conversion boundary between a raw UCIInfo.Score and product logic, producing a mate-aware centipawn value at an explicit point of view. The annotation sweep does not use it — extractEval above is the annotation path's normalizer — but DrillLeniency.leniencyVerdict(best:played:marginCp:) and the repertoire audit take their evaluations through it:

public enum PointOfView { case sideToMove, opponentOfSideToMove }
public struct Evaluation { public let centipawns: Int; public let mateIn: Int?
                           public var isMate: Bool }   // mateIn != nil

EngineScoreAdapter.evaluation(from: score, pointOfView: .sideToMove)           // Evaluation
EngineScoreAdapter.evaluation(from: info,  pointOfView: .opponentOfSideToMove) // Evaluation?

Both overloads default to .sideToMove (the UCI convention). The UCIInfo overload returns nil for a score-less line rather than fabricating a cp 0. .opponentOfSideToMove negates both centipawns and mateIn, through a saturating negation that maps Int.min to Int.max — a malformed cp Int.min line must not turn a sign flip into an arithmetic trap.

docs.title: MultiPV carriers
docs.text: Type Shape Notes PositionEval bestMoveUCI, scores: [Int: UCIInfo.Score], moves: [Int: String] 1-based rank keys; bestScore falls back to .cp(0); secondBestScore / secondBestMoveUCI return rank 2 or nil. moves defaults to [:] — rank 2's move is only needed as evidence the second PV completed RecklessLine rank, evalText, bestMoveSAN, bestMoveUCI Identifiable on rank (1 = best); evalText is pre-formatted White-POV. Origin/target squares are derived by the caller, not stored

docs.title: Classifying a ply
docs.text:
computeAnnotations(inputs:evals:startIsWhite:) produces one NodeAnnotationResult per ply. For ply i:

guard i < evals.count - 1 else break   // short eval array truncates, never crashes

moverIsWhite = (i % 2 == 0) == startIsWhite
wpBefore     = winProbability(evals[i].bestCp)
wpAfter      = 1 - winProbability(evals[i + 1].bestCp)  // after-position is the OPPONENT's POV
wpDrop       = max(0, wpBefore - wpAfter)

gap          = winProbability(evals[i].bestCp) - winProbability(evals[i].secondBestCp)
               or 0 when secondBestCp is nil

opponentMissed = i > 0
              && (winProbability(evals[i - 1].bestCp) - (1 - wpBefore)) >= 0.10
              && wpBefore > 0.55

matchedBestMove = !bestMoveUCI.isEmpty
               && UCIParser.uciToMove(bestMoveUCI, in: positionBefore) == move

winProbability(cp) = 1 / (1 + exp(-0.00368208 * cp))

The complement on wpAfter is the step worth remembering: the engine evaluated the position after the move, where it is the opponent's turn, so its score is already from the opponent's POV. Subtracting from 1 puts both numbers back in the mover's frame, the only frame wpDrop is meaningful in.

gap is the single input separating the positive glyphs from "no annotation": with MultiPV 1 it is always 0, and .brilliant, .great, .best, .excellent and .good all become unreachable — every row in the positive band requires gap >= 0.03 or more. opponentMissed fires when the previous mover let a winning position slip and the current mover is still comfortable — it upgrades a .mistake or .dubious to .miss, and is always false at ply 0. An unparseable or empty best-move UCI silently yields matchedBestMove == false.

Each ply also borrows two numbers from AccuracyAggregator:

classifyMoveQuality(wpDrop:playedBestMove:)     moveAccuracy(wpBefore:wpAfter:)
    playedBestMove → .best  (overrides all)         drop = max(0, wpBefore - wpAfter) * 100
    wpDrop >= 0.20 → .blunder                       raw  = 103.1668 * exp(-0.04354 * drop)
    wpDrop >= 0.10 → .mistake                              - 3.1668
    wpDrop >= 0.05 → .inaccuracy                    →      min(100, max(0, raw))
    wpDrop >= 0.02 → .good
    otherwise      → .excellent

The glyph cascade and the quality cascade share the 0.20 / 0.10 / 0.05 / 0.02 thresholds but are separate outputs written to separate fields.

Available from the command line: fianchetto-cli accuracy.

docs.title: The glyph cascade
docs.text:
classifyGlyph(wpDrop:wpBefore:wpAfter:gap:playedBestMove:opponentMissed:involvesSacrifice:absEvalCp:) is an ordered decision table. The first matching row wins.

── error band (worst first) ────────────────────────────────────────────
 1  wpDrop >= 0.20                                       → .blunder
 2  wpDrop >= 0.10                → opponentMissed ? .miss : .mistake
 3  wpDrop >= 0.05                → opponentMissed ? .miss : .dubious

── positive band ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    notAlreadyWinning = wpBefore < 0.75

 4  wpDrop < 0.02 && gap >= 0.15 && absEvalCp < 50_000
    && notAlreadyWinning && involvesSacrifice            → .brilliant
 5  wpDrop < 0.02 && gap >= 0.08 && wpBefore < 0.40      → .great
 6  wpDrop < 0.02 && gap >= 0.08 && wpBefore < 0.55
    && wpAfter > 0.60                                    → .great
 7  playedBestMove && gap >= 0.03                        → .best
 8  wpDrop < 0.02 && gap >= 0.03                         → .excellent
 9  wpDrop < 0.05 && gap >= 0.06                         → .good
10  otherwise                                            → nil

Note

The ordering is part of the contract, not just the thresholds. Row 7 precedes row 8, so a played best move with a 0.05 gap is .best and not .excellent; the error band precedes everything, so a sacrifice that also drops 0.25 win probability is a .blunder, never a .brilliant. The absEvalCp < 50_000 guard on row 4 excludes mate-sentinel positions, and notAlreadyWinning excludes flashy moves in already-won games.

classifyGlyph never returns .interesting; that case exists for hand annotation and is handled by the consensus severity ladder below.

docs.title: Sacrifice detection
docs.text:
involvesSacrifice(positionBefore:positionAfter:) is the Sendable-safe home of the logic; the involvesSacrifice(node:) overload delegates to it.

moverColor    = positionBefore.activeColor
opponentColor = moverColor.opposite

for index in 0..<64:
    sq = Square.fromIndex(index)
    skip unless positionAfter[sq] is a moverColor piece
    skip if piece.type is .king or .pawn
    skip unless MoveGenerator.isSquareAttacked(sq, by: opponentColor, in: positionAfter)

    if NOT MoveGenerator.isSquareAttacked(sq, by: moverColor, in: positionAfter)
        → true                     // attacked and undefended

    pawnDir = (opponentColor == .white) ? -1 : 1
    for df in [-1, 1]:
        pawnSq = Square(file: sq.file + df, rank: sq.rank + pawnDir)
        if pawnSq.isValid and holds an opponentColor pawn
            → true                 // capturable by a less-valuable piece

→ false

Kings are excluded because they cannot be sacrificed; pawns because a hanging pawn is too common to be evidence of anything. The second branch catches the defended-but-pawn-attacked case: a defended knight en prise to a pawn is still material down after the exchange. pawnDir points back toward the opponent pawn that would capture — the inverse of that pawn's push direction.

docs.title: Point of view
docs.text:
engineEval is stored White-POV: positive means White is better, regardless of whose turn it is. Two helpers move between frames, both applying moverIsWhite = (plyIndex % 2 == 0) == startIsWhite — no-op for White, negate for Black:

AnnotationKernel.whitePovCpToMoverPov(whitePovCp, plyIndex: i, startIsWhite: true)
AnnotationKernel.whitePovEvals(evals, startIsWhite: true)  // [Double], same length, [0] = start

Because the ±100 000 mate sentinel carries only a sign, cp values and mate values round-trip through the negation identically. The first is what ConsensusKernel.compare needs; the second builds the eval chart.

The eval string comes from EvalFormat.formatCentipawnsNoDistance(cp:isMate:):

isMate → cp >= 0 ? "M" : "-M"          // bare, no distance
else   → sign + (|cp| / 100) + "." + zero-padded (|cp| % 100)
         e.g. +1.34, -0.21             // pure integer arithmetic

The mate distance is omitted on purpose: bestCp encodes only that a forced mate exists, so printing M5 there would be a fabrication.

docs.title: Writing results back
docs.text:
public struct AnnotationComputeInput: Sendable {
    public let positionBefore: Position
    public let positionAfter: Position
    public let move: Move
}

public struct NodeAnnotationResult: Sendable {
    public let glyph: MoveAnnotation?
    public let moveQuality: MoveQuality
    public let moveAccuracy: Double        // 0…100
    public let engineBestMoveUCI: String?  // nil when the before-position had none
    public let engineEval: String?         // White-POV, e.g. "+1.34" / "-M"
}

AnnotationComputeInput exists purely so the classify pass never touches the non-Sendable MoveNode: extract on the node's actor, cross the boundary with value types, come back with NodeAnnotationResult values.

applyAnnotations(_:to:game:) clears before it writes — it first nils setAnnotation(nil, on:), moveQuality, moveAccuracy, engineBestMoveUCI, and engineEval on every node in mainLine, then writes results in order, breaking at i >= mainLine.count. Re-annotating therefore always starts from a clean slate, even when the new result array is shorter than the old one.

annotateNodes(mainLine:evals:game:startIsWhite:) wraps extract → compute → apply in one call. Use the split form whenever the classify pass must run off the main actor.

docs.title: End to end
docs.text:
import ChessCore
import FianchettoKit

struct StockfishAnnotator: PositionEvaluator {
    let session: MyUCISession    // your transport; the kernel never sees it

    func evaluate(fen: String) async -> AnnotationEval? {
        var infoByRank: [Int: UCIInfo] = [:]
        var bestMoveUCI = ""
        for await line in session.search(fen: fen, multiPV: 2, movetimeMs: 500) {
            if let info = UCIInfoParser.parseInfo(line) {
                guard info.score != nil else { continue }
                infoByRank[info.multiPV] = info
            } else if line.hasPrefix("bestmove") {
                bestMoveUCI = UCIInfoParser.parseBestMove(line) ?? ""
                break
            }
        }
        return AnnotationKernel.extractEval(fromRankedInfos: infoByRank,
                                            bestMoveUCI: bestMoveUCI)
    }
}

// positions[0] = start, positions[i+1] = after ply i
let mainLine = game.mainLine
let positions = [game.startPosition] + mainLine.map { $0.positionAfter }
let startIsWhite = game.startPosition.activeColor == .white

guard let evals = await AnnotationDriver.collectEvals(
    positions: positions,
    evaluator: StockfishAnnotator(session: session),
    onProgress: { done, total in print("\(done)/\(total)") }
) else { return }   // cancelled, or the engine stopped responding

// Pure classify pass — safe off the main actor.
let inputs = mainLine.map {
    AnnotationComputeInput(positionBefore: $0.positionBefore,
                           positionAfter: $0.positionAfter,
                           move: $0.move)
}
let results = AnnotationKernel.computeAnnotations(inputs: inputs,
                                                  evals: evals,
                                                  startIsWhite: startIsWhite)

// Write pass, on the model's actor.
AnnotationKernel.applyAnnotations(results, to: mainLine, game: game)

// The eval chart uses the White-POV projection of the same array.
let chart = AnnotationKernel.whitePovEvals(evals, startIsWhite: startIsWhite)

docs.title: Two-engine consensus
docs.text:
ConsensusKernel is the pure logic behind the Stockfish + Reckless features: higher-confidence annotations, and "critical moments".

public struct EngineRead: Sendable, Equatable {
    public let cp: Int
    public let isMate: Bool
    public let bestMoveUCI: String
    public var winProbability: Double   // mates clamp to 1.0 / 0.0 by sign
}

The mate clamp is what makes two engines comparable when they disagree about mate distance: both reads collapse to the same 1.0 or 0.0, so "mate in 4 vs mate in 6" contributes no gap at all. The caller must supply both reads in the same POV — both White-POV or both mover-POV — which is what whitePovCpToMoverPov(_:plyIndex:startIsWhite:) is for.

compare(a, b, criticalGap: 0.15)

gap      = |a.winProbability - b.winProbability|
sameMove = a.bestMoveUCI == b.bestMoveUCI && !a.bestMoveUCI.isEmpty
critical = gap >= criticalGap                        // 0.15 by default
        || (!sameMove && gap >= criticalGap * 2/3)   // 0.10 when they differ
confidence = (sameMove && gap < 0.05) ? .high : (critical ? .low : .medium)

Confidence is high | medium | low; Verdict carries agreeOnBestMove, winProbGap, confidence, and isCriticalMoment. Disagreeing on the move lowers the bar for "critical" by a third, because a move disagreement is itself evidence the position is double-edged.

Glyph reconciliation runs on a signed severity ladder:

Annotation .brilliant .great .best, .excellent .good, .interesting nil .dubious .miss, .mistake .blunder Severity +4 +3 +2 +1 0 −1 −2 −3 
reconcileAnnotation(a, b)
    severity(a) == 0 or severity(b) == 0 → nil   // one engine finds it unremarkable
    signs differ (one good, one bad)     → nil   // no confident call
    otherwise → abs(sa) <= abs(sb) ? a : b       // the LESS emphatic one; ties keep a

An emphatic !! or ?? survives only when both engines are that emphatic, which is exactly what cuts single-engine false positives.

Verdicts persist per ply through ConsensusRecord(ply:agree:winProbGap:confidence:critical:) — ply is 0-based, and confidence is a plain String holding Confidence.rawValue so a decoder does not need FianchettoKit. ConsensusJSON is the plain-array codec in the EvalJSON style: encode returns "[]" on any failure, decode returns [] for empty or malformed input. Neither throws.

Why raw centipawns are comparable here

Both Stockfish and Reckless emit normalized centipawns — Reckless's normalize_to_cp mirrors Stockfish's NormalizeToPawnValue — so the single AccuracyAggregator.winProbability(cp:) logistic applies to both on the same win-expectancy scale and no engine-specific calibration is needed. Comparing on win probability rather than raw cp is still the robust axis, because it compresses the tails where cp scales diverge most.

docs.title: Provenance and cache validity
docs.text:
Evaluation arrays alone do not record which engine produced them or how much search was spent, so treating any non-empty array as current silently reused Stockfish results after a switch to Reckless. AnnotationProvenance is the durable identity of one primary annotation run:

Field Meaning schemaVersion envelope version — stamped by init, currently 1 contractVersion version of the orientation / MultiPV / classification / persistence contract owned by AnnotationKernel, currently 1 engine AnnotationEngineKind engineRevision engine + wrapper + network identity, as a string searchKind .movetimeMilliseconds or .depth searchLimit the numeric budget for that kind multiPV lines requested includesConsensus whether glyphs were reconciled with a second engine

Both version fields are stamped by init, never supplied by the caller.

satisfies(required) — true only when ALL hold

    schemaVersion   == 1  and  required.schemaVersion   == 1
    contractVersion == 1  and  required.contractVersion == 1
    engine          == required.engine
    engineRevision  == required.engineRevision
    searchKind      == required.searchKind
    searchLimit     >= required.searchLimit          ← the only inequality
    multiPV         == required.multiPV
    includesConsensus || !required.includesConsensus  ← one-way superset

A deeper or longer search may stand in for a weaker request; nothing else relaxes. Results never cross engine, network-revision, search-kind, MultiPV, or contract boundaries. Consensus is a strict superset of a primary-only run, so a consensus result satisfies a primary-only requirement but not the reverse — and recordingConsensus() returns a copy with includesConsensus set to true once reconciliation succeeds.

let required = AnnotationProvenance(
    engine: .stockfish,
    engineRevision: "sf17-nnue-b1a57f",
    searchKind: .movetimeMilliseconds,
    searchLimit: AnnotationKernel.annotateMovetime(batch: true, thoroughness: "fast"),
    multiPV: 2,
    includesConsensus: false
)

// storedProvenanceJSON is whatever String? your persistence layer kept next to
// the eval array.
if let stored = AnnotationProvenanceCodec.decode(storedProvenanceJSON),
   stored.satisfies(required) {
    // Cached evals are honest for this request — skip the sweep.
} else {
    // Missing, malformed, over 4 096 bytes, a future schema, or a different
    // configuration: all treated as stale, never as current.
    let json = AnnotationProvenanceCodec.encode(required.recordingConsensus())
}

Structural validity is enforced by the codec at both ends: versions exactly 1, engineRevision non-empty, at most 512 UTF-8 bytes and entirely printable ASCII (0x20...0x7e), 0 < searchLimit <= 60_000, and 0 < multiPV <= 32. encode uses JSONEncoder with .sortedKeys — a stable string for equality and diffing — and returns "" for a structurally invalid value or an encode failure. decode returns nil for nil/empty input, input over 4 096 UTF-8 bytes, malformed JSON, or a decoded value that fails structural validity.

docs.title: Display mapping
docs.text:
The glyph, name, and tint live in FianchettoKit so the two apps cannot drift again — they already had, once, on "Dubious" vs "Inaccuracy".

MoveAnnotation displayGlyph displayName displayRGB .brilliant !! Brilliant (0.0, 0.67, 0.67) .great △ Great (0.35, 0.55, 0.71) .best ✓ Best (0.55, 0.72, 0.30) .excellent ✓ Excellent (0.55, 0.72, 0.30) .good ! Good (0.45, 0.65, 0.50) .interesting !? Interesting (0.45, 0.70, 0.45) .dubious ?! Inaccuracy (0.90, 0.64, 0.45) .miss ✕ Miss (0.85, 0.55, 0.30) .mistake ? Mistake (0.90, 0.50, 0.15) .blunder ?? Blunder (0.80, 0.20, 0.20) MoveQuality .best .excellent .good .inaccuracy .mistake .blunder displayName Best Excellent Good Inaccuracy Mistake Blunder displayRGB (0.0, 0.67, 0.45) (0.30, 0.72, 0.40) (0.60, 0.72, 0.30) (0.95, 0.70, 0.20) (0.95, 0.50, 0.20) (0.80, 0.20, 0.20)

.dubious renders as "Inaccuracy" deliberately: the glyph stays ?! in move lists, but the word users read matches the MoveQuality.inaccuracy band it corresponds to. Blunder red is 0.80 in both tables, on purpose.

displayRGB is a plain (red: Double, green: Double, blue: Double) triple in 0…1 — no SwiftUI import — so the values are usable from tests, from a headless tool, and from a non-Apple port. Each app wraps it in its own Color.

docs.title: Companion value types
docs.text:
MaterialBalance.compute(from:) derives captured material and White's point advantage from a Position, kings excluded:

pieceOrder     = [.queen, .rook, .bishop, .knight, .pawn]   // canonical display order
startingCounts = queen 1, rook 2, bishop 2, knight 2, pawn 8
pieceValues    = queen 9, rook 5, bishop 3, knight 3, pawn 1

missing(type, color) = max(0, startingCounts[type] - present(type, color))
capturedByWhite = missing for Black,  capturedByBlack = missing for White
whiteAdvantage  = Σ whiteCount·value − Σ blackCount·value

The max(0, …) clamp is what makes it promotion-safe: three queens on the board produce zero captured queens, not −2. Only non-zero entries are stored.

ClockCore holds the precise remaining times; the display throttle, Timer, and @Observable wrapper stay per-platform.

var clock = ClockCore(minutes: preset.minutes, increment: preset.increment)
clock.start(color: .white)
clock.advance(byElapsed: 0.1)     // @discardableResult -> isExpired
clock.switchTurn()                // increment to the mover, THEN flip
clock.stop()
clock.reset()                     // both sides to initialSeconds, .white to move

switchTurn() and advance(byElapsed:) are both no-ops unless isRunning. Increment lands on the side that just moved, before the flip. advance subtracts from the active side clamped by max(0, …). loser checks White first, so a double-flag reports .white. forceRemaining(white:black:) exists only under #if DEBUG and writes the precise fields — the wrappers' observable display fields are lagging copies and cannot expire the clock.

TimePreset is the shared time-control table (rawValue is the display string and also the id):

Case .bullet1_0 .bullet2_1 .blitz3_0 .blitz3_2 .blitz5_0 .blitz5_3 .rapid10_0 .rapid15_10 .classical30_0 Raw 1+0 2+1 3+0 3+2 5+0 5+3 10+0 15+10 30+0 category Bullet Bullet Blitz Blitz Blitz Blitz Rapid Rapid Classical minutes 1 2 3 3 5 5 10 15 30 increment 0 1 0 2 0 3 0 10 0

Maia-side results. GameAnalysis holds MoveResult(moveIndex:playerMoveRank:playerMoveProbability:) values with 0-based ranks and derives accuracy (share with rank 0), top3Accuracy (share with rank in 0..<3), and averageProbability — all three return 0 for an empty moveResults. GuessEloResult carries whiteElo and blackElo as Int?, where nil means no estimate was produced for that side. EloKernel.bestElo(from:) is the argmax over a [Float: Double] map of Elo bucket → per-game average log-likelihood, returning Int(best.key) and nil for an empty map; the key is Float to match the CoreML output key type, and dictionary iteration order leaves ties unspecified. The Maia scoring path these summarize is reachable headlessly through fianchetto-cli maia, but the CLI emits its own JSON rows — these three types have no CLI surface today.

docs.title: Running it headless
docs.text:
Seam Reachable today annotateMovetime(batch:thoroughness:) fianchetto-cli annotate AnnotationDriver.collectEvals(positions:evaluator:onProgress:) fianchetto-cli annotate AnnotationKernel.terminalEval(for:) fianchetto-cli annotate (via the driver) AnnotationKernel.extractEval(fromRankedInfos:bestMoveUCI:) fianchetto-cli annotate AnnotationKernel.whitePovEvals(_:startIsWhite:) fianchetto-cli annotate AccuracyAggregator.winProbability / moveAccuracy / classifyMoveQuality fianchetto-cli accuracy classifyGlyph, computeAnnotations, applyAnnotations kernel-only ConsensusKernel, ConsensusRecord, ConsensusJSON kernel-only AnnotationProvenance / AnnotationProvenanceCodec kernel-only involvesSacrifice, MaterialBalance, ClockCore, TimePreset kernel-only

fianchetto-cli annotate emits the White-POV eval array per game — the same array the app's eval chart draws — and stops the whole run on the first engine timeout, matching collectEvals's abort semantics exactly. Everything marked kernel-only is pure and Sendable, so it is directly unit-testable without an engine; it simply has no CLI surface yet.

docs.title: Library backup & collections
docs.text:
One portable JSON export format that the Apple app and the Android (Skip/SkipFuse) port both read and write, plus the shared kernels that validate it, stream it out in bounded memory, collapse duplicate games, and decide when a soft-deleted collection's rows may physically go away.

Everything on this page is Foundation + ChessCore. There is no UI, no SwiftData, and no CloudKit dependency, so a command-line tool can run the same validator the app runs before it touches a user's library.

docs.title: Where the pieces live
docs.text:
File What it owns LibraryBackup.swift the portable value model, LibraryBackupCategories, LibraryBackupAncillaryOverlay, and LibraryBackupCodec (config + the whole validation boundary) LibraryBackupAuthoredAdapter.swift the one canonical authored-history view: identity candidates, ownership, row canonicalization, the two reconciler plans LibraryBackupReplayableSource.swift actor-confined streaming input and LibraryBackup.Game.replaySemanticFingerprint LibraryBackupStreamingEncoder.swift incremental encode, ValidatedStream, StreamingError, byte accounting LibraryBackupSettingPolicy.swift the 40-key curated setting registry, its domains, and RatingChartWindow LibraryGameReconciliation.swift lossless collapse of duplicate physical game rows CollectionLifecycle.swift / CollectionCleanupPolicy.swift soft-deletion generations and the resumable cleanup state machine CollectionOwnerResolver.swift "whose archive is this?" from an explicit username or by inference

The prose specification of the file itself is docs/BACKUP_FORMAT.md in the repo; the types below are what that document tracks.

docs.title: The portable value model
docs.text:
LibraryBackup is the top-level Codable value. currentSchemaVersion is 1.

Row type Carries Collection name, source, username, lastSyncDate, includeInOpeningBook, orderIndex, dateCreated, games Game the persisted, non-derived fields of a stored game (see below) Game.Enrichment the authored/engine-derived payload that may enrich an already-present game PersonalTrapRow fen, correctMoveUCI, userActualMoveUCI, gapCp, halfMoveIndex, sourceGameID, sourceOpeningName, detectedAt TrapScanRecord sourceGameID, trapsFound, scannedAt, optional canonical manifestJSON Repertoire / RepertoireMoveRow header (color, repertoireID, anchorFEN, anchorLineSAN) and its moves (positionKey, san, comment, auditDismissed, annotation) AuditCacheRow / PunishCacheRow one cached audit/punish generation per color, keyed by colorRaw + fingerprint SyncedBlobRow the single-row-per-logical-key projection of the CloudKit-synced JSON blob store (key, dataJSON, updatedAt, replicaID) SyncedBlobConflictRow a lossless sidecar holding the alternate payloads for one duplicated blob key; the chosen active value stays in syncedBlobs SettingRow / SettingValue one curated preference and its typed value (bool / int / string)

Three rules make this shape survivable across two platforms and several app versions:

date is a string. LibraryBackup.Game.date is the PGN yyyy.MM.dd field, not an ISO-8601 Date. It stays opaque; nothing in the codec parses it.

Additive fields are optionals, never a schema bump. repertoires is [Repertoire]? and auditCaches, punishCaches, syncedBlobs, syncedBlobConflicts and settings are optionals defaulted to nil, so a backup written before those sections existed still decodes. The same applies inside rows: annotationMateDistancesJSON, annotationProvenanceJSON, boardArrowsJSON, consensusJSON, maiaLogLikesJSON and maiaTargetEvidenceV1JSON on Game, anchorLineSAN on Repertoire, annotation on RepertoireMoveRow.

exportedAt is truncated at construction. Both LibraryBackup.init and LibraryBackupAncillaryOverlay.init push the date through canonicalExportDate, so the in-memory value matches what the ISO-8601 encoding can actually carry and signed byte metadata cannot claim precision the payload does not have.

canonicalExportDate(d) = Date(timeIntervalSince1970: d.timeIntervalSince1970.rounded(.down))

docs.title: Enrichment overlay
docs.text:
Game.Enrichment exists so a restore can add analysis and notes to a game that is already present without disturbing its PGN identity. overlayingNonEmpty(from:) is the merge:

live.overlayingNonEmpty(from: backup)

  every String / String? field:  a non-empty incoming value wins;
                                 nil or empty NEVER erases live data

  annotationProvenanceJSON:      replaced by the backup's value only when the
                                 backup carries a non-empty annotationEvalsJSON
                                 or secondBestEvalsJSON — otherwise a
                                 provenance-less older backup would misattribute
                                 the live engine's numbers

  maiaTargetEvidenceV1JSON:      MaiaBackfillPolicy.preferredTargetEvidence(
                                     live:incoming:)   — resolved by policy,
                                 not by emptiness

Available from the command line: fianchetto-cli maia produces the same target-evidence vector the backup carries in maiaTargetEvidenceV1JSON.

docs.title: Categories are a wire contract
docs.text:
LibraryBackupCategories is an OptionSet naming the selective import/export categories. Persisted restore journals store its rawValue, so the bit assignments must never diverge by platform:

.games 1 << 0   .repertoires 1 << 1   .traps    1 << 2
.caches 1 << 3  .progress    1 << 4   .settings 1 << 5
.all = the union of all six

docs.title: SettingValue's hand-written Codable
docs.text:
Swift synthesizes Codable for an associated-value enum as a single-key object with the payload nested under _0. SettingValue hand-writes exactly that shape rather than relying on synthesis:

{"string": {"_0": "blue"}}

Skip/SkipFuse transpilation of a synthesized associated-value enum Codable is a portability risk, and the "obvious" flat form {"string":"blue"} would fail to decode on iOS. The decoder probes for bool, then int, then string, and throws DecodingError.dataCorrupted when none is present.

docs.title: The codec
docs.text:
LibraryBackupCodec is the single source of truth for encoder/decoder configuration and for the entire validation boundary.

makeEncoder():  outputFormatting     = [.withoutEscapingSlashes, .sortedKeys]
                dateEncodingStrategy = .iso8601
makeDecoder():  dateDecodingStrategy = .iso8601

.sortedKeys is load-bearing. Without it swift-foundation emits object keys in hash-seed-dependent order that varies across processes — and, on the macOS 15 runner's older Foundation, across encode() calls within one process. Any consumer that treats the encoded bytes' SHA-256 as a payload identity (backup publication dedup and retention do) would see an unchanged library as "changed" on re-encode. Canonical key order makes that hash a true content identity.

Note
