Sorted keys are a guarantee about what this encoder writes, not a requirement on what a reader may assume. Object key order is deliberately not part of the portable contract — parse by key, and compare documents semantically rather than byte-for-byte across implementations.

Entry point Use decodeSupported(_:) decode a complete backup and enforce the whole boundary decodeSupportedWithAuthoredProjection(_:) the same, returning a ValidatedDecode that carries the authored projection encodeSupported(_:) validate, then encode, then re-check the payload ceiling validateSupported(_:) enforce the boundary on an already-decoded value decodeSupportedAncillaryOverlay(_:) / encodeSupportedAncillaryOverlay(_:) / validateSupportedAncillaryOverlay(_:) the game-free overlay equivalents authoredLogicalGameIDs(in:) every authored logical ID the backup's game rows safely own maxPayloadBytes the pre-decode byte ceiling, 512 * 1024 * 1024

A bare JSONDecoder is never a safe entry point. Swift's Codable intentionally ignores unknown fields, so a future-schema backup would appear to restore successfully while silently dropping everything the reader does not know about — which is exactly what the schema gate below exists to prevent.

docs.title: 1. Schema gate
docs.text:
schemaVersion <  1                        → ValidationError.invalidSchema(found:)
schemaVersion >  currentSchemaVersion (1) → ValidationError.unsupportedSchema(found:supported:)

docs.title: 2. Payload ceiling
docs.text: maxPayloadBytes = 512 * 1024 * 1024 (536,870,912). It is checked before JSONDecoder runs in both decode paths, after encoding in both encode paths, and incrementally during streaming. An unbounded document would otherwise let a malformed multi-gigabyte file multiply its footprint inside the decoder and terminate the process.

docs.title: 3. Resource ceilings
docs.text:
Every one of these throws resourceLimitExceeded(section:limit:). Running totals use addingReportingOverflow and reject on overflow rather than wrapping.

Section Limit collections 4,096 games 250,000 across the whole backup collection.games 100,000 in any one collection repertoires 10,000 auditCaches, punishCaches 10,000 each repertoireMoves 500,000 summed across repertoires personalTraps, trapScanRecords 250,000 each syncedBlobs 1,000,000 syncedBlobConflicts 500,000 syncedBlobAlternates 1,000,000 aggregate syncedBlobAlternatesPerKey 63 for a compact-head key, 10,000 otherwise settings 512 syncedBlob 16 MiB per dataJSON (primary rows and alternates alike)

The per-key alternate limit is chosen by record kind:

perKeyLimit = AuthoredBlobRecordCodec.kind(of: conflict.key) == .compactHead
    ? AuthoredBlobRecordCodec.maximumCompactHeadAlternates   // 64 - 1 = 63
    : 10_000

A sidecar excludes the active row, which is why the compact-head sidecar ceiling is one below maximumCompactHeadCandidates (64).

docs.title: 4. Field-size classes
docs.text:
small fields ≤ 65,536 UTF-8 bytes
  collection name / source / username     → invalidCollection(index:field: "metadata")
  game gameID                             → invalidGame(..., field: "identity")
  game white, black, date, event, result,
       opening, tagsJSON                  → invalidGame(..., field: "metadataSize")

large fields ≤ 8,388,608 bytes (8 MiB)
  moveText, annotationEvalsJSON, secondBestEvalsJSON, userNotes,
  annotationMateDistancesJSON, annotationProvenanceJSON, boardArrowsJSON,
  consensusJSON, maiaLogLikesJSON, maiaTargetEvidenceV1JSON
                                          → invalidGame(..., field: "payloadSize")

blob fields ≤ 16,777,216 bytes (16 MiB)
  every syncedBlobs[].dataJSON and every conflict alternate dataJSON
                                          → resourceLimitExceeded(section: "syncedBlob",
                                                                  limit: 16777216)

also: collection.orderIndex >= 0 and game.orderIndex >= 0

Empty identity strings are deliberately tolerated — older stores contain unnamed collections and empty game IDs, which import adapters repair with their canonical fallbacks.

The same per-game pass enforces two authored-identity invariants:

userNotes must pass AuthoredNotesValue.validatePersistenceRepresentation
                                    → invalidGame(..., field: "userNotesRepresentation")

marker = AuthoredGameIdentity.marker(in: game.tagsJSON)
  throws                            → invalidGame(..., field: "authoredIdentityMarker")
  present:
    seed = GameDedup.authoredIdentityKey(
               white:, black:, date:, result:, event:, opening:,
               moveText:, tagsJSON:,
               strippingDerivedAnnotations:
                   PreparedGameData.computeIsAnnotated(
                       evalsJSON: game.annotationEvalsJSON,
                       moveText: game.moveText))
    markerBySeed[seed] exists and differs
                                    → invalidGame(..., field: "authoredIdentityMarkerConflict")

docs.title: 5. Chess semantics
docs.text:
Non-authored semantic validation runs in this order, and every check is real chess rather than a shape assertion:

Rows Checks personalTraps fen parses as a Position; both correctMoveUCI and userActualMoveUCI are legal in that position (UCIParser.uciToMove); gapCp >= 0; halfMoveIndex >= 0 trapScanRecords trapsFound >= 0 and manifestState != .malformed repertoires color is exactly "white" or "black"; every non-nil repertoireID is unique; anchorFEN parses anchorLineSAN a non-empty line requires an anchor, and its whitespace-split SAN replayed from Position.initial() (PGNParser.parseMove + MoveGenerator.applyMoveUnchecked) must end on the anchor's positionKey repertoire moves positionKey parses as a FEN, san parses in that position, and a present annotation is a valid MoveAnnotation(rawValue:) auditCaches, punishCaches colorRaw is "white"/"black" and at most one row per color syncedBlobs keys non-empty and unique syncedBlobConflicts key non-empty and unique, alternates non-empty, and a primary row with the same key exists in syncedBlobs settings key non-empty and unique, and LibraryBackupSettingPolicy.accepts(row)

docs.title: The ValidationError vocabulary
docs.text:
The typed cases are a triage guide — each one names the section, the index, and where relevant the failing field.

Case Reached by payloadTooLarge(limit:) pre-decode, post-encode, or a streaming chunk resourceLimitExceeded(section:limit:) any count or blob-size ceiling invalidSchema(found:) / unsupportedSchema(found:supported:) the schema gate invalidCollection(index:field:) collection metadata size or negative orderIndex invalidGame(collectionIndex:gameIndex:field:) identity, metadataSize, payloadSize, userNotesRepresentation, authoredIdentityMarker, authoredIdentityMarkerConflict invalidPersonalTrap(index:field:) fen, correctMoveUCI, userActualMoveUCI, numericRange invalidTrapScanRecord(index:) negative count or a malformed manifest invalidRepertoireColor(index:color:), duplicateRepertoireID(_:), invalidRepertoireAnchor(index:), invalidRepertoireAnchorLine(index:), invalidRepertoireMove(repertoireIndex:moveIndex:field:) the repertoire pass invalidAuditCache(index:), invalidPunishCache(index:) bad color or a second row for one color duplicateSyncedBlobKey(_:), invalidSyncedBlobConflict(key:) blob key uniqueness and sidecar/primary pairing invalidAuthoredBlob(key:), orphanedAuthoredBlob(logicalGameID:) the authored adapter and the reconciler (below) duplicateSettingKey(_:), invalidSettingValue(_:) the settings pass

Authored failures are translated into those last two cases. AdapterError and every AuthoredBackupReconciler.PlanError map onto invalidAuthoredBlob(key:) except PlanError.orphanedLogicalGameID, which becomes orphanedAuthoredBlob(logicalGameID:). Three sentinel keys appear when the failure has no single row to blame: "<game-identity>" for an AuthoredGameIdentity.IdentityError, "<validated-projection>" for a re-projection source mismatch, and "<authored>" for anything else.

docs.title: Authored history
docs.text:
LibraryBackupAuthoredAdapter is the one canonical authored view of a backup. It builds identity candidates, resolves logical-ID ownership, moves every accepted causal row onto its promoted canonical lineage, and runs the reconciler twice.

Each backup game becomes a candidate addressed by GameOffset(collectionIndex:gameIndex:) (Comparable, ordered by collection then game):

identitySeed        = GameDedup.authoredIdentityKey(
                          white:, black:, date:, result:, event:, opening:,
                          moveText:, tagsJSON:,
                          strippingDerivedAnnotations:
                              PreparedGameData.computeIsAnnotated(
                                  evalsJSON:, moveText:))
semanticRemoteGameID = GameIdentity.persistedRemoteID(
                          gameID: game.gameID,
                          link:   tags["Link"],
                          site:   tags["Site"])

project(_:) then runs a deliberately two-pass validation:

1. backup-ONLY ownership over those candidates, and
   AuthoredBackupReconciler.plan(.init(
       primaryRows:           authored rows as written,
       conflictSidecars:      authored sidecars as written,
       allowedLogicalGameIDs: backupOnlyOwnership.aliases))

   The boundary is backup-only on purpose: a live marker or semantic remote ID
   must never make an otherwise-orphan source row look valid. This pass is what
   still catches duplicate sidecars, mismatched keys, immutable-revision
   sidecars, and sidecars with no primary row — all of which could disappear
   once two aliases regroup under one canonical key.

2. canonicalize every primary row and every sidecar alternate through
   canonicalized(_:canonicalLogicalIDByAlias:); regroup alternates under the
   canonical key and emit keys in sorted order.

3. AuthoredBackupReconciler.plan(.init(
       primaryRows:           canonical rows,
       conflictSidecars:      regrouped sidecars,
       allowedLogicalGameIDs: Set(ownership.logicalIDByCandidate.values)))

   Alias-collision history conflicts surface here, before any live store is
   inspected or mutated.

Row canonicalization decodes with AuthoredBlobRecordCodec.decode(key:dataJSON:), looks the decoded logicalGameID up in canonicalLogicalIDByAlias defaulting to itself, rekeys when the canonical ID differs, and re-emits (storageKey(for:), canonicalDataJSON(for:), row.updatedAt). Unknown IDs stay unknown by design, so the reconciler's ownership check rejects them instead of laundering an orphan into the selected set. Any failure becomes AdapterError.invalidRecord(key:).

Projection.allowedLogicalGameIDs holds canonical lineages only. Aliases are transit and storage names, not independent game ownership.

When live candidates are supplied to project(_:additionalCandidates:), backup rows are tagged CombinedID(kind: 0, index:) and live candidates CombinedID(kind: 1, index:) in one combined ownership replay, so a marker carried by either side can promote deterministic aliases without accepting two logical histories.

docs.title: The unforgeable shortcut
docs.text:
reprojectValidated(_:validatedBase:additionalCandidates:) lets a restore adapter skip the raw structural plan it already paid for. The authorization is a fileprivate let validatedSourceProof on Projection — unreachable to callers, so a projection you construct yourself, or one obtained from a different backup, cannot authorize the shortcut and throws AdapterError.validatedProjectionSourceMismatch.

The proof is recomputed with constant retained storage over exactly the inputs that can affect authored ownership:

PortableSHA256, every field length-prefixed:

  "library-authored-source:v1"
  collections.count
  per collection: games.count
    per game: white, black, date, result, event, opening,
              moveText, tagsJSON, gameID, annotationEvalsJSON
  "primary"
    per syncedBlobs row where AuthoredBlobRecordCodec.isAuthoredKey(key):
        "row", key, dataJSON, framed(updatedAt)
    primaryRows.count
  "sidecars"
    per authored conflict row:
        "sidecar", key, alternates.count,
        per alternate: dataJSON, framed(updatedAt)
    conflictSidecars.count

framed(nil)  = "nil"
framed(date) = "date", String(date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate.bitPattern, radix: 16)

Progress, repertoire and cache fields are excluded because they cannot affect authored ownership.

docs.title: Bounded-memory export
docs.text: JSONEncoder only hands back a payload-sized Data. The streaming encoder keeps that encoder authoritative for object fields and scalar representation but replaces aggregate arrays with incrementally emitted contents, so a 250,000-game library never needs a second full encoded copy in memory.

docs.title: Actor-confined input
docs.text:
LibraryBackupCodec.ReplayableSource is a per-collection header plus a declared gameCount plus a replay closure that yields one LibraryBackup.Game at a time. It carries ordinary, non-@Sendable closures so a persistence actor may capture its native model objects — and it therefore declares:

@available(*, unavailable, message: "ReplayableSource is actor-confined")
extension LibraryBackupCodec.ReplayableSource: Sendable {}

It must be consumed synchronously by the actor that created it.

Every traversal accumulates a field-framed replay proof:

"library-replay-games:v1"
collections.count
per collection:  collectionIndex, declared gameCount
  per game:      collectionIndex, gameIndex, <replay fields>

<replay fields> — the same framing as LibraryBackup.Game.replaySemanticFingerprint
                  (domain "library-backup-game-replay:v2"):
  orderIndex,
  white, black, date, event, result, opening, moveText, tagsJSON, gameID,
  annotationEvalsJSON, secondBestEvalsJSON, userNotes,
  then each of annotationMateDistancesJSON, annotationProvenanceJSON,
  boardArrowsJSON, consensusJSON, maiaLogLikesJSON, maiaTargetEvidenceV1JSON
  framed as "some" + value, or "nil"

The proof is field-framed rather than JSON-byte-based so harmless key-ordering changes cannot look like source mutation. Validation and the final write must reproduce the same proof, which is what stops a stateful source from validating one game set and encoding another. A collection that yields a different number of games than it declared throws StreamingError.replayCollectionCountMismatch(collectionIndex:expected:actual:); a later pass that proves different content throws .replaySourceChanged.

docs.title: The shell splice
docs.text:
shell = the same value with every aggregate array emptied
        (optional arrays via `map { _ in [] }`, so nil-vs-empty presence survives)

for each aggregate property p:
    marker = "\"p\":[]" located in the encoded shell with Data.range(of:)
    absent → StreamingError.incompatibleArrayShell(property: p)
             — and NO shell bytes have been emitted yet
    insertion index = the index just before the closing ]

sort insertion points ascending, then for each:
    write shell[cursor ..< index]
    write the elements, comma-separated, each encoded independently
    cursor = index
finally write shell[cursor...]

Nested shells apply the same trick to collections → games, repertoires → moves, and syncedBlobConflicts → alternates.

docs.title: Byte accounting and the proof
docs.text:
maximumStreamingChunkBytes = 64 * 1_024 = 65,536

for each chunk of at most 65,536 bytes:
    (next, overflow) = byteCount.addingReportingOverflow(chunk.count)
    overflow || next > maxPayloadBytes → ValidationError.payloadTooLarge(limit:)
    emit(chunk)            ← the sink first
    hasher.update(chunk)   ← then the proof
    byteCount = next

Only bytes the sink accepted participate in the returned ExactByteProof(byteCount:sha256:); a throwing sink owns disposal of its partial staging target.

Warning

Validation completes before the first byte is emitted, but a sink failure or a late aggregate size failure can still leave a partial stream on disk. Always stream into a discardable staging file and publish it only after the call returns successfully.

validatedStream(for:) runs validateSupported and hands back a Sendable ValidatedStream, so the expensive semantic work can happen before a file-coordination lock is taken. Each write(emit:) returns its own proof, because key order is not a stable part of the portable contract.

// Prepare before the lock; write inside it.
let stream = try LibraryBackupCodec.validatedStream(for: backup)

let handle = try FileHandle(forWritingTo: stagingURL)
let proof = try stream.write { chunk in
    try handle.write(contentsOf: chunk)
}
try handle.close()

guard proof.isStructurallyValid(
    maximumByteCount: LibraryBackupCodec.maxPayloadBytes
) else { throw ExportError.badProof }

try FileManager.default.replaceItemAt(publishedURL, withItemAt: stagingURL)

Streaming straight from a persistence actor, without materializing the games:

let source = LibraryBackupCodec.ReplayableSource(
    exportedAt: Date(),
    collections: storedCollections.map { stored in
        .init(
            name: stored.name,
            source: stored.source,
            username: stored.username,
            lastSyncDate: stored.lastSyncDate,
            includeInOpeningBook: stored.includeInOpeningBook,
            orderIndex: stored.orderIndex,
            dateCreated: stored.dateCreated,
            gameCount: stored.games.count,
            replayGames: { visit in
                // One game in memory at a time. `prepared` is the adapter's own
                // PreparedGameData projection; the enrichment is built beside it
                // so PGN identity and authored payload never get mixed up.
                for row in stored.games {
                    try visit(LibraryBackup.Game(
                        prepared: row.prepared,
                        enrichment: .init(
                            annotationEvalsJSON: row.annotationEvalsJSON,
                            secondBestEvalsJSON: row.secondBestEvalsJSON,
                            userNotes: row.userNotes
                        )
                    ))
                }
            }
        )
    },
    personalTraps: traps,
    trapScanRecords: scans,
    repertoires: repertoires,
    didEncodeGame: { completed, total in
        progress.update(completed: completed, total: total)
    }
)

let proof = try LibraryBackupCodec.streamSupported(source) { chunk in
    try handle.write(contentsOf: chunk)
}

docs.title: Ancillary overlays
docs.text:
LibraryBackupAncillaryOverlay is a prior export's ancillary rows without its game graph. collections and repertoires are absent from the encoded shape: a persistence adapter already owns their live representation, and decoding last export's whole game graph just doubles the dominant memory cost.

init(projecting:) builds one from a full backup; ancillaryEnvelope produces a compatibility LibraryBackup with empty collections and nil repertoires for existing ancillary merge kernels.

Warning

An overlay envelope is not a backup and must never be published directly. Authored ownership cannot be checked without game rows, so overlay authored rows must go through AuthoredBackupReconciler against the adapter's live ownership before anything is emitted or persisted.

docs.title: Curated settings
docs.text:
LibraryBackupSettingRegistry.definitions holds 40 canonical, platform-neutral keys. Each is a LibraryBackupSettingDefinition (key + LibraryBackupSettingRule); platform adapters keep only their own physical UserDefaults / SharedPreferences mapping.

20 bools — soundEnabled, hapticsEnabled, autoAnnotateOnImport, consensusAnnotation, pref.secondOpinion, updateGamesFullSweep, explorerAutoFollow, drillAutoAdvance, drillShowArrows, punishDrillSkipMastered, reviewQuizSkipMastered, trapDrillSkipMastered, endgameEndToEnd, otbAutoFlip, showCoordinates, showLegalMoveHints, autoICloudBackupEnabled, defaultStockfishEval, defaultMaiaEval, confirmGameDelete.

9 bounded ints (inclusive ranges):

Key Domain drillSessionSize 1…100 checkmateIntensity 0…3 missedMateMaxN 2…10 punishTopK 2…8 punishOpponentElo 800…2,400 autoICloudBackupRetention 1…30 masteryThreshold 2…10 tacticsSwingThreshold 50…1,000 stockfishDepthLimitPersisted 0…128

11 bounded strings, every one .string(maximumUTF8Bytes: 256) — boardTheme, pieceSet, explorerDatabase, annotateThoroughness, annotationEngine, tacticsMode, drillStrictness, evalDisplayFormat, libraryGameSort, ratingChartWindow, otbLastTimeControl.

LibraryBackupSettingPolicy.accepts(row)
    = LibraryBackupSettingRegistry.definition(forKey: row.key)?
          .rule.accepts(row.value) ?? true

  UNKNOWN key   → accepted (forward compatibility; adapters apply only keys in
                  their own physical mapping)
  KNOWN key     → the value kind must match exactly, and:
                     .int(minimum: a, maximum: b)  (a...b).contains(value)
                     .string(maximumUTF8Bytes: n)  value.utf8.count <= n

normalizedPortableRow(_:) adds one canonicalization on top. Older Apple builds stored lowercase rating-window values while Android stored display labels ("3M", "6M", "1Y", "All"):

normalizedPortableRow(row)
    !accepts(row)                      → nil
    row.key != "ratingChartWindow"     → row unchanged
    row.key == "ratingChartWindow":
        value must be .string, and RatingChartWindow(storedValue:) must map it
        (trim whitespace/newlines, lowercase)
        → re-emitted as the canonical lowercase rawValue: "3m" | "6m" | "1y" | "all"
        → unmappable value returns nil, so the row is DROPPED rather than
          persisted as a picker selection no UI can represent

RatingChartWindow also exposes shortLabel (3M/6M/1Y/All) and monthOffset (-3, -6, -12, nil for .all). It conforms to Identifiable but has no UI dependency.

let safeRows = (backup.settings ?? [])
    .compactMap(LibraryBackupSettingPolicy.normalizedPortableRow)

docs.title: Duplicate-game reconciliation
docs.text:
LibraryGameReconciliation plans the lossless collapse of multiple physical rows that are the same logical game. It is persistence-agnostic: preview and execution consume the same immutable Plan — update each survivor from originalGame to mergedGame, then delete exactly deleteIndices. Keeping the survivor preimage also lets an undo adapter restore both sides.

let plan = LibraryGameReconciliation.plan(games: rows)

if plan.hasChanges {
    for survivor in plan.survivors {
        store.update(at: survivor.inputIndex, to: survivor.mergedGame)
    }
    store.delete(at: plan.deleteIndices)   // already sorted ascending
}
print("\(plan.deletionCount) rows collapsed, \(plan.retainedIndices.count) kept")

docs.title: Grouping
docs.text:
BaseProof = (normalizedPersistedID, logicalKey, coreFingerprint, positionSequence)

fingerprint          = GameDedup.compositeKey(white:black:date:result:event:opening:
                                              moveText:tagsJSON:
                                              strippingDerivedAnnotations:)
stableID             = GameIdentity.stableID(gameID:link:site:contentID: fingerprint)
logicalKey           = GameDedup.key(gameID: stableID, compositeKey: fingerprint)
authoritative        = (logicalKey is .remoteID)
coreFingerprint      = authoritative ? "" : fingerprint
positionSequence     = GameDedup.positionSequenceProof(game.moveText,
                                                       tagsJSON: game.tagsJSON)
normalizedPersistedID = GameIdentity.canonicalProviderID(game.gameID)
                     ?? PreparedGameData.normalizedGameID(game.gameID)

Two field incidents shaped that key:

  • Canonical, not raw, persisted ID. normalizedGameID only trims, so "https://www.chess.com/game/live/171115885774" and "chesscom:171115885774" stay different strings for the same game — while logicalKey, which runs canonicalProviderID, already says they are one. The raw form defeated the canonical one: same logical key, different base proof, never grouped. Latent until commit 73a36701 (2026-07-11) made imports write the canonical form; 96 such pairs were then found in the owner's library, confirmed by identical final-position FENs.
  • Authoritative groups drop text sensitivity. When the logical key is .remoteID, coreFingerprint is stored as the empty string. One chess.com game held three rows, two carrying {[%clk 0:09:54.6] +0.4; best Nf3} and one carrying only {[%clk 0:09:54.6]}. Identical moves, clocks and remote ID — but strippingDerivedAnnotations is computed per row and did not reduce those comments to the same text, so the fingerprints differed, the rows never entered one group, and a completed repair pass left 542 rows untouched. The position-sequence proof is what actually guards this. Content-keyed groups keep the strict fingerprint, since text identity is their only evidence.

docs.title: Subsumption
docs.text:
A survivor may absorb a source only if it can prove nothing is lost:

target.subsumes(source, authoritativeIdentity:)

both modes first require
    source.boardArrows == nil || source.boardArrows == target.boardArrows
        — board arrows are user-authored; never delete a row carrying arrows the
          survivor does not already hold

authoritative (recognized remote ID: provably one online game):
    if source.hasGlyphedMainLine && source.derivedMoveText == nil
       && source.glyphLine != target.glyphLine        → NOT subsumed
        — nothing but the user's hand explains glyphs on a row with no engine
          annotation in either format
    for f in {derivedMoveText, annotationEvals, secondBestEvals,
              mateDistances, annotationProvenance, consensus}:
        require source.f == nil || target.f != nil     ← PRESENCE only
        — a redundant engine run is droppable; a COMPLEMENTARY partial analysis
          is never lost, and the survivor keeps its own values

content-keyed:
    for the same six fields: require source.f == nil || source.f == target.f

docs.title: Search and survivor preference
docs.text:
Rows are projected once and bucketed by BaseProof; only buckets with more than one member enter candidate work. Projection and exact-base grouping are linear in total input; the deterministic greedy reconciliation is at most cubic within one conflicting group. Inside a group the loop runs while more than one index remains available, evaluating each still-available index as a survivor over the order-preserving filtered list — never Set or Dictionary iteration order.

isPreferred(lhs, over: rhs) — first difference wins:
  1. isAnnotated          annotated beats unannotated
  2. positionRichness     higher   (non-nil count among the 7 position fields)
  3. enrichmentRichness   higher   (positionRichness + non-empty note + non-empty maia)
  4. derivedDepth         higher   moveText.count
                                 + annotationEvalsJSON.count
                                 + secondBestEvalsJSON.count
                                 + annotationMateDistancesJSON?.count ?? 0
                                 + annotationProvenanceJSON?.count ?? 0
                                 + consensusJSON?.count ?? 0
                                 + merged.maiaTargetEvidenceV1JSON?.count ?? 0
  5. orderIndex           LOWER
  6. deleteIndices.count  higher
  7. survivorIndex        lower

The independent userNotes / maiaLogLikesJSON pair is chosen without a Cartesian product:

choices = { (target.note, target.maia) }
        ∪ { (target.note ?? s.note, target.maia ?? s.maia) for each observed pair s }
        ∪ { (most frequent note-only, most frequent maia-only) }
              — only when the target has NEITHER; ties break to the
                lexicographically smaller value

deletionCount(choice) = freq(nil,  nil)
                      + freq(note, nil)   if choice.note != nil
                      + freq(nil,  maia)  if choice.maia != nil
                      + freq(note, maia)  if both != nil

discard deletionCount == 0, then maximize:
  enrichmentRichness, then deletionCount, then choicePrecedes
  (nil sorts before any value, then lexicographic on note, then on maia)

maiaTargetEvidenceV1JSON folds over the deleted rows through
MaiaBackfillPolicy.preferredTargetEvidence(live:incoming:)

docs.title: Collection lifecycle
docs.text:
CollectionLifecycle encodes soft deletion for a CloudKit-synchronized collection in one signed Int64 per parent, so an existing store adopts the protocol without a destructive migration.

parent scalar:  0        active LEGACY generation (CollectionLifecycle.legacyGeneration)
                positive active generation
                negative deletion generation (a soft tombstone)
child scalar:   the non-negative active generation it was attached to;
                a MISSING child value means legacy generation 0

parentState(lifecycleVersion: v)
    v >= 0 → .active(generation: v)
    v <  0 → .deleted(generation: v == Int64.min ? Int64.max : -v)
             — avoids trapping on abs(Int64.min); an extreme value is
               conservatively the largest representable tombstone

activeGeneration(lifecycleVersion: v) = v >= 0 ? v : nil
    — nil for a tombstone, so a writer cannot stamp a child into a deleted parent

childDisposition(parentLifecycleVersion: v, childIncarnation: c)
    g = c ?? 0
    g < 0                       → .deferred   (outside the wire contract: quarantine,
                                               never destroy on an invalid value)
    parent .active(p):  g == p  → .visible
                        g <  p  → .stale
                        g >  p  → .deferred
    parent .deleted(d): g <= d  → .stale      (the tombstone wins at its own
                                               generation too)
                        g >  d  → .deferred   (a reactivation parent record has
                                               not arrived yet)

isSettledActiveRelationship(parentLifecycleVersion:childIncarnations:)
    requires a non-nil activeGeneration and EVERY child .visible

deletionVersion(after: v)      .deleted        → v          (idempotent on retry)
                               .active(g)      → -(g + 1)
                               .active(Int64.max) → -Int64.max
reactivationVersion(after: v)  generation == Int64.max ? nil : generation + 1

Only .visible children belong in user-facing reads. .stale children under a deleted parent are what become eligible for physical cleanup; .deferred means CloudKit delivered records out of order — retain and retry.

docs.title: The rollout gate
docs.text:
CollectionLifecycle.SoftDeletionReadiness keeps activation explicit so that merely adding lifecycle fields to the local model cannot switch on a wire protocol older peers cannot interpret:

permitsProtocolV1 = productionSchemaReady && compatibleClientFloorReady

.disabled        = (false, false)
.protocolV1Ready = (true,  true)

docs.title: Resumable cleanup
docs.text:
CleanupSnapshot is the exact parent tombstone plus child-generation set observed at an import-idle boundary. Children are canonicalized on init — sorted by token, then incarnation with nil ordering before any value — so equality is deterministic across fetch order, process launches, and JSON round trips.

CleanupSnapshot.isStructurallyValid   (fail closed on every count)
    parentToken non-empty and <= 8 * 1_024 UTF-8 bytes
    tombstoneVersion < 0 and != Int64.min
    children.count <= maximumCleanupChildrenPerCollection (250,000)
    every child token non-empty, <= 8 * 1_024 UTF-8 bytes, and unique

isExactSubset(of: authorized)
    both snapshots structurally valid
    same parentToken and same tombstoneVersion
    children.count <= authorized.children.count
    every child ∈ Set(authorized.children)

staleChildTokens and deferredChildTokens are derived through CollectionLifecycle.childDisposition, so read filtering and cleanup authority never drift apart.

requiredStableCleanupObservations = 2

cleanupTransition(previous:current:observationToken:)

  current invalid, or observationToken empty / > 8 * 1_024 bytes,
  or the retained observation invalid    → .blocked, previous observation preserved
  previous == nil                        → .observing, count 1, action .none

  .observing, SAME lastObservationToken
      identical snapshot                 → no-op (.none)      ← a replayed
                                                                notification never
                                                                increments stability
      different snapshot                 → restart .observing
  .observing, NEW token
      different snapshot                 → restart .observing
      identical, no stale children       → .quiescent, .none
      identical, stale children          → .cleaning,
                                           .cleanup(authorization: current,
                                                    eligibleChildTokens:
                                                        current.staleChildTokens)
  .cleaning
      current not an exact subset of the retained authorization
                                         → restart .observing  ← any ADDITION or
                                                                 generation change
      stale set empty                    → .quiescent, .none
      otherwise                          → re-issue the RETAINED authorization for
                                           another bounded batch
  .quiescent
      snapshot changed                   → restart .observing
      identical                          → no-op (.none)

Missing children while .cleaning are safe: a prior batch or a peer already removed them, which is exactly why resumption uses subset containment rather than equality.

let snapshot = CollectionLifecycle.CleanupSnapshot(
    parentToken: parentToken,
    tombstoneVersion: CollectionLifecycle.deletionVersion(after: parentVersion),
    children: childRows.map {
        .init(token: $0.token, incarnation: $0.incarnation)
    }
)

let transition = CollectionLifecycle.cleanupTransition(
    previous: storedObservation,      // CleanupObservation?
    current: snapshot,
    observationToken: completedImportPassID
)
storedObservation = transition.nextObservation

switch transition.action {
case .none:
    break
case .cleanup(let authorization, let eligibleChildTokens):
    try deleteChildren(eligibleChildTokens, authorizedBy: authorization)
case .blocked:
    // Fail closed: preserve every row for manual diagnosis.
    logger.error("cleanup blocked for \(parentToken)")
}

CleanupObservation.isStructurallyValid ties the counter to the phase: stableObservationCount == 1 in .observing, == 2 in .cleaning, and == 2 with an empty stale set in .quiescent.

docs.title: Owner resolution
docs.text:
Online imports carry an authoritative account username. Ordinary PGN files do not, but a typical personal archive has one player in every game and varying opponents. CollectionOwnerResolver recognizes only that unambiguous shape.

normalized(name) = name.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).lowercased()

resolve(explicitUsername:games:)
    explicit = normalized(explicitUsername)
    explicit non-empty                                        → explicit
    games.count < 2                                           → nil
    for every game:
        white = normalized(game.white), black = normalized(game.black)
        either empty, either a placeholder, or white == black → nil
        intersection ∩= {white, black}; empty                 → nil   (early bail)
    intersection.count == 1                                   → that name
    otherwise                                                 → nil

placeholders (8): "?", "unknown", "anonymous", "anon",
                  "white", "black", "player", "computer"

Every other shape fails closed, so an opponent, a placeholder, a match collection, or a one-off PGN cannot be mistaken for the user.

let owner = CollectionOwnerResolver.resolve(
    explicitUsername: collection.username,      // "" for a plain PGN import
    games: parsed.map {
        CollectionOwnerResolver.GamePlayers(white: $0.white, black: $0.black)
    }
)

docs.title: Using it headlessly
docs.text:
A complete validate-and-rehash pass needs nothing but Foundation and ChessCore:

import FianchettoKit

let data = try Data(contentsOf: url)

// Decode + schema gate + resource ceilings + chess semantics + authored plans.
let validated = try LibraryBackupCodec.decodeSupportedWithAuthoredProjection(data)
let backup = validated.backup

print("schema \(backup.schemaVersion), exported \(backup.exportedAt)")
print("\(backup.collections.count) collections, "
    + "\(backup.collections.reduce(0) { $0 + $1.games.count }) games")
print("\(validated.authoredProjection.allowedLogicalGameIDs.count) authored lineages")

// Canonical re-encode: sorted keys make this SHA-256 a content identity.
let canonical = try LibraryBackupCodec.encodeSupported(backup)
let identity = ExactByteProof(bytes: canonical)
print(identity.sha256, identity.byteCount)

// Every logical ID the game rows safely own, aliases included.
let owned = try LibraryBackupCodec.authoredLogicalGameIDs(in: backup)

fianchetto-cli today exposes the engine and estimation seams — fianchetto-cli annotate, estimate, maia, accuracy, project, track — and none of the backup kernels yet. The natural additions, each one file conforming to CLICommand over the APIs above, would be:

Proposed subcommand Would wrap JSON-lines contract backup-validate decodeSupportedWithAuthoredProjection(_:) one line per input file: {"path", "ok", "error"} with the ValidationError case name and its associated values backup-proof streamSupported(_:emit:) into /dev/null {"path", "byte_count", "sha256"} — the publication identity without writing a copy reconcile LibraryGameReconciliation.plan(games:) games in, {"survivors": [{"input_index", "delete_indices"}], "delete_indices"} out settings LibraryBackupSettingPolicy.normalizedPortableRow(_:) rows in, normalized rows out plus a dropped reason owner CollectionOwnerResolver.resolve(explicitUsername:games:) {"white", "black"} lines in, one {"owner"} line out lifecycle CollectionLifecycle.cleanupTransition(previous:current:observationToken:) a snapshot per line, the transition's phase and action per line

Those are proposals, not shipped commands. The library APIs they would call are the ones documented above, and all of them run without a UI.

docs.title: Maia policy model
docs.text: Maia is a human-move-prediction network conditioned on a player's rating. This page covers the three pure files FianchettoKit owns around it: the tensor codec (Maia3Encoding), the backfill policy that decides what gets scored and how the result is persisted (MaiaBackfillPolicy and the free function logSoftmaxAt), and the rank tiering used to color move lists (MaiaRankStyle).

docs.title: What lives in the kit
docs.text:
The kit owns every decision; it owns no inference. Model loading and the tensor round-trip stay in the app — MaiaEngine/CoreML on Apple, an ONNX/LiteRT backend on Android — and both call the same encoder, the same qualification gate, and the same envelope codec.

Type What it does Maia3Encoding Position → 768-float token tensor, Move → policy index, raw logits → EngineAnalysis MaiaBackfillPolicy game/position eligibility, owner side, opponent conditioning, the Elo grid, the persisted JSON envelope MaiaBackfillPolicy.ScoringContext the resolved per-game contract (side, elo_oppo, source, move-list fingerprint) MaiaBackfillPolicy.TargetEvidence the decoded 11-point vector the Elo estimator consumes MaiaBackfillPolicy.OpponentConditioning which elo_oppo contract a persisted vector was scored under logSoftmaxAt(_:idx:) numerically stable log-softmax at one policy index — the per-position accumulation term MaiaRankStyle rank → .best / .good / .moderate / .poor display tier

Maia3Encoding.swift and MaiaBackfillPolicy.swift import Foundation and ChessCore and nothing else; MaiaRankStyle.swift imports only Foundation. There is no CoreML, no SwiftData, and no SwiftUI in this path, so all of it runs headless.

docs.title: Maia3Encoding — board encoding
docs.text:
encodeTokens(position:) produces 64 squares × 12 piece planes = 768 floats, one-hot, always from White's perspective. When Black is to move the board is turned around: ranks are flipped and piece colors are swapped. Files are never mirrored.

isBlack = (position.activeColor == .black)

for rank in 0..<8, file in 0..<8:
    actualRank = isBlack ? (7 - rank) : rank
    piece      = position[Square(file: file, rank: actualRank)]   // skip if empty
    pieceColor = isBlack ? piece.color.opposite : piece.color
    featureIdx = pieceFeatureIndex(piece.type) + (pieceColor == .white ? 0 : 6)
    sqIdx      = rank * 8 + file
    tokens[sqIdx * 12 + featureIdx] = 1.0

pieceFeatureIndex:  pawn 0, knight 1, bishop 2, rook 3, queen 4, king 5
                    (+6 for the side that is black after the perspective swap)

let tokens = Maia3Encoding.encodeTokens(position: .initial())
tokens.count                              // 768
tokens.filter { $0 == 1.0 }.count         // 32 — one per piece on the board

Exactly one feature is set per occupied square, so the number of 1.0 entries is the piece count: 32 for the starting position.

docs.title: Maia3Encoding — the policy map
docs.text:
The policy head is 4352 wide: 4096 from-to pairs plus 256 promotion slots.

Move kind Index Range Regular fromSq * 64 + toSq 0–4095 Promotion 4096 + fromFile * 32 + toFile * 4 + promoIndex 4096–4351 
isBlack  = (activeColor == .black)
fromRank = isBlack ? (7 - move.from.rank) : move.from.rank
toRank   = isBlack ? (7 - move.to.rank)   : move.to.rank

if move.promotion == nil:
    fromSq = fromRank * 8 + move.from.file
    toSq   = toRank   * 8 + move.to.file
    index  = fromSq * 64 + toSq
else:
    index  = 4096 + move.from.file * 32 + move.to.file * 4 + promotionIndex

promotionIndex:  queen 0, rook 1, bishop 2, knight 3   (anything else → 0)

Worked example — e2e4 as White. e2 is file 4, rank 1, so fromSq = 1 * 8 + 4 = 12; e4 is file 4, rank 3, so toSq = 3 * 8 + 4 = 28; the index is 12 * 64 + 28 = 796.

let e2e4 = Move(from: Square(algebraic: "e2")!, to: Square(algebraic: "e4")!, piece: .pawn)
Maia3Encoding.policyIndex(for: e2e4, activeColor: .white)   // 796

The promotion branch ignores the mirrored ranks

fromRank and toRank are computed for both branches, but the promotion index is built from files only. A promotion therefore lands on the same index whichever side plays it — promotions are already rank-determined (7 → 8 after mirroring), so the rank carries no information here.

docs.title: Maia3Encoding — decoding the output
docs.text:
decodeOutput(moveLogits:valueLogits:position:topK:) turns raw head outputs into a ChessCore EngineAnalysis. It throws in two cases:

Condition Thrown moveLogits.count < 4352 EngineError.predictionFailed("Missing or invalid policy output. Size: \(count)") the position has no legal moves EngineError.noLegalMoves

The value head is optional and is only read when valueLogits is non-nil with at least 3 entries. Its three logits are [loss, draw, win] from the side-to-move's perspective, and the decoder always emits white-POV:

e0, e1, e2 = exp(Double(v0)), exp(Double(v1)), exp(Double(v2))   // Double: Android
sum        = e0 + e1 + e2                                        // lacks the Float
stmLoss, drawProb, stmWin = e0/sum, e1/sum, e2/sum               // exp overload

activeColor == .black  →  .winDrawLoss(win: stmLoss, draw: drawProb, loss: stmWin)
otherwise              →  .winDrawLoss(win: stmWin,  draw: drawProb, loss: stmLoss)

The policy is softmaxed over the legal moves only, not over all 4352 outputs, with the usual max subtraction for stability:

legal   = MoveGenerator.legalMoves(for: position)         // decodeOutput throws if empty
logits  = [ policyLogits[policyIndex(m)] for m in legal ] // indices past the array end are skipped
maxL    = max(logits)
p_i     = exp(l_i - maxL) / Σ_j exp(l_j - maxL)

sort descending by p, take prefix(topK)

Each survivor becomes an EngineAnalysis.ScoredMove(move:notation:probability:) with SAN from MoveGenerator.algebraicNotation(for:in:).

var logits = [Float](repeating: 0, count: 4352)
logits[796] = 10                                      // e2e4

let analysis = try Maia3Encoding.decodeOutput(
    moveLogits: logits,
    valueLogits: nil,
    position: .initial(),
    topK: 3
)
analysis.topMoves.first?.notation                     // "e4"
analysis.topMoves.first?.probability                  // softmax over the 20 legal moves

docs.title: logSoftmaxAt — the accumulation term
docs.text:
public func logSoftmaxAt(_ logits: [Float], idx: Int) -> Double?

A free function (not a member of either enum). It is the single term the backfill sums: the log-probability the network assigned to the move the player actually made.

guard 0 <= idx < logits.count                     else nil
maxValue = logits[0];  guard maxValue.isFinite    else nil
for value in logits:  guard value.isFinite else nil;  maxValue = max(maxValue, value)

exponentialSum = Σ exp(Double(value) - Double(maxValue))
result         = Double(logits[idx]) - (Double(maxValue) + log(exponentialSum))
guard result.isFinite                             else nil

It returns nil in three situations: an out-of-range index, any non-finite logit anywhere in the array, and a non-finite result. These iOS finite-validation semantics are the canonical ones — Android previously returned -Double.infinity for out-of-range indices and did not validate the logits at all, which turned a broken inference into a plausible-looking very negative number.

One nil aborts the whole vector

Callers propagate nil as a throw and discard all 11 grid points. Zeroing or skipping a single term would bias exactly one Elo point of the sweep relative to the other ten, and — worse — would produce a structurally valid envelope that never requeues. Failing the whole game leaves it eligible for a retry.

docs.title: The backfill contract
docs.text:
Constant Value eloGrid [600, 800, 1000, 1200, 1400, 1600, 1800, 2000, 2200, 2400, 2600] expectedVectorLength eloGrid.count — 11 neutralOpponentElo 1_500 (Float) trainedOpponentEloRange 400...3_200 targetEvidenceContractID "maia3-v4.1-owner-moves-elo-sweep-v1" targetEvidenceSchemaVersion 1

eloGrid is not a literal in the policy: it is read at runtime from EloCalibrationData.v41ensembleModel(forRawTC: TimeControlClass.blitz.rawValue)?.eloGrid so the policy cannot drift from the calibration artifact it feeds. The literal array above is the fallback if that model is somehow unavailable.

targetEvidenceContractID binds persisted evidence to a model and a serving contract. Bump it whenever the model's outputs, the Elo grid, the move scope, or the conditioning semantics change — every stored envelope then fails validation and requeues by itself. The current Apple .mlpackage component hashes and the Android ONNX hash are pinned against this same value in ModelContracts/maia-target-evidence-assets.registry; updating a hash there without bumping the contract is safe only for byte-level repackaging whose numerical equivalence was established explicitly.

docs.title: Which games get scored
docs.text:
isCandidateForBackfill = statisticsEnabled && hasAnnotationEvals && !hasMaiaVector
isEligibleForBackfill  = isCandidateForBackfill && isEligible(tc:)

isCandidateForBackfill(statisticsEnabled:hasAnnotationEvals:hasMaiaVector:) is the cheap pre-check the scheduler runs before parsing PGN tags; isEligibleForBackfill(statisticsEnabled:hasAnnotationEvals:hasMaiaVector:tc:) is the same thing once the time-control tag has been classified.

statisticsEnabled is the user-facing "Include in My Stats" collection toggle — persisted as includeInOpeningBook on Apple and includeInStats on Android. Maia vectors refine only the statistics projection, so an opted-out collection must never consume model inference on either platform.

Time control isEligible(tc:) Estimator route .bullet true v4.1 ensemble (with Maia) .blitz true v4.1 ensemble .rapid true v4.1 ensemble .classical true v4.1 ensemble — Maia contributes +115.6 Elo in the fit .correspondence false v2 binned median, no Maia refinement

docs.title: Which positions get scored
docs.text:
qualifiesForInference(plyIndex:legalMoveCount:)  ==  plyIndex >= 8 && legalMoveCount > 2

That is an exact mirror of the training collector's gate in collect_ensemble_corpus.py (if ply >= skip_plies and legal > 2: with skip_plies = 8): skip the first eight half-moves, which are mostly memorized book, and skip near-forced positions, where any model looks like any human. plyIndex is 0-indexed — ply 0 is the position before White's first move — and the legal count comes from MoveGenerator.legalMoves(for:).count, which is strict-legal and matches python-chess.

Two walks apply the gate over a parsed main line:

// Every qualifying position in the game.
MaiaBackfillPolicy.qualifyingPositions(from: parsed.moves)

// Only positions where the account owner is to move — the shape the training
// corpus used (one record per player).
MaiaBackfillPolicy.qualifyingPositions(from: parsed.moves, playerColor: .white)

Both return [(plyIndex: Int, move: Move, positionBefore: Position)] in ply order. The owner-only overload exists because scoring both sides would mix the opponent's playing style into the cached vector; the fitted coefficients assume one player's moves.

Golden fixtures

Ruy Lopez, Morphy Defence — 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 a6 4. Ba4 Nf6 5. O-O Be7 6. Re1 b5 7. Bb3 d6 8. c3 O-O (16 plies) yields 8 qualifying positions at plies 8–15 with legal-move counts [27, 30, 25, 30, 25, 30, 27, 33]. The White-only walk returns plies [8, 10, 12, 14], Black-only [9, 11, 13, 15]. Scholar's mate (1. e4 e5 2. Qh5 Nc6 3. Bc4 Nf6 4. Qxf7#, 7 plies) yields zero — every ply is below the threshold.

docs.title: Owner side and opponent conditioning
docs.text:
scoringContext(white:black:username:source:moveText:tagsJSON:whiteElo:blackElo:) resolves everything needed to score one game, or returns nil if the game is out of domain.

1. Domain gate (from tagsJSON via GameTagCodec.decode):
      SetUp != "1"  AND  FEN tag empty  AND  Variant empty or "standard"
2. Owner side:  PieceColor.ofUser(white:black:username:)
      nil when the username matches neither player, or both → return nil
3. Opponent Elo + conditioning:
      exactOpponentElo = (playerColor == .white) ? blackElo : whiteElo
      canonicalSource  = OnlineGameSourceIdentity.canonical(source)
                         ?? (trimmed+lowercased source, or "unknown" if empty)

      if canonicalSource == "lichess"
         && exactOpponentElo != nil
         && (400...3_200).contains(exactOpponentElo):
             opponentElo = Float(exactOpponentElo);  conditioning = .exactLichess
      else:
             opponentElo = 1_500;                    conditioning = .neutralLichessPrior

The rating-scale argument is the whole reason for the branch. Maia's elo_oppo input was trained on Lichess ratings; a Chess.com rating of 1650 is not the same strength as a Lichess 1650, and feeding it in would silently shift the conditioning. The neutral 1500 prior is deliberately explicit and stays until a provider calibration can map other scales onto Maia's domain.

ScoringContext field Meaning playerColor which side is the account owner opponentElo the elo_oppo value to feed the model ownerUsername trimmed + lowercased source canonicalized ("lichess", "chesscom", else lowercased or "unknown") opponentConditioning .exactLichess or .neutralLichessPrior inputFingerprint 64 hex characters binding the evidence to the exact move list

The fingerprint is a PortableSHA256.Hasher fed length-prefixed UTF-8 in a fixed order:

tokens      = PGNParser.tokenize(PreparedGameData.normalizeForParsing(moveText))
mainLineSAN = PGNParser.flatMoves(from: tokens)

update(lengthPrefixedUTF8: targetEvidenceContractID)
update(lengthPrefixedUTF8: playerColor == .white ? "white" : "black")
for san in mainLineSAN: update(lengthPrefixedUTF8: san)
hexDigest()                                    // 64 hex characters

Length prefixing means no concatenation of adjacent SAN tokens can collide, and including the contract ID means a contract bump changes every fingerprint.

docs.title: Driving a sweep
docs.text:
The scorer is app-side, but its shape is fixed by this policy: encode each qualifying owner position once, then sweep elo_self across the 11 grid points with elo_oppo held at the context's value.

let parsed = PGNParser.mainLineSnapshot(fromMoveText: moveText)

guard let context = MaiaBackfillPolicy.scoringContext(
    white: game.white,
    black: game.black,
    username: account.username,
    source: collection.source,
    moveText: moveText,
    tagsJSON: game.tagsJSON,
    whiteElo: whiteElo,
    blackElo: blackElo
) else { return }                       // out of domain, or ambiguous account

let qualifying = MaiaBackfillPolicy.qualifyingPositions(
    from: parsed.moves,
    playerColor: context.playerColor
)
guard !qualifying.isEmpty else {
    // Terminal receipt: valid game, but no owner move survives the filters.
    persist(MaiaBackfillPolicy.encodeNoQualifyingOwnerMoves(context: context))
    return
}

// Encode once, reuse across all 11 grid points.
let encodings: [(policyIndex: Int, tokens: [Float])] = try qualifying.map { entry in
    let tokens = Maia3Encoding.encodeTokens(position: entry.positionBefore)
    let index = Maia3Encoding.policyIndex(
        for: entry.move,
        activeColor: entry.positionBefore.activeColor
    )
    guard tokens.count == 768, (0..<4352).contains(index) else { throw ScoringError.invalidEncoding }
    return (policyIndex: index, tokens: tokens)
}

var logLikes = [Double](repeating: 0, count: MaiaBackfillPolicy.expectedVectorLength)
for (gridIndex, eloSelf) in MaiaBackfillPolicy.eloGrid.enumerated() {
    for encoding in encodings {
        let logits = try infer(encoding.tokens, Float(eloSelf), context.opponentElo)
        guard let term = logSoftmaxAt(logits, idx: encoding.policyIndex) else {
            throw ScoringError.missingOutput          // abort the whole vector
        }
        logLikes[gridIndex] += term
    }
}

let json = MaiaBackfillPolicy.encodeTargetEvidence(
    logLikes,
    context: context,
    eligibleMoveCount: encodings.count
)

encodeTargetEvidence(_:context:eligibleMoveCount:) returns nil — refusing to persist — unless the vector has exactly 11 entries, every entry is finite, and eligibleMoveCount > 0.

Available from the command line: fianchetto-cli maia.

docs.title: The evidence envelope
docs.text:
The persisted JSON is a 12-key envelope, not a bare array:

{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "contractID": "maia3-v4.1-owner-moves-elo-sweep-v1",
  "moveScope": "account-owner-only",
  "playerColor": "white",
  "ownerUsername": "magnus",
  "source": "lichess",
  "opponentConditioning": "exact-lichess-opponent",
  "opponentElo": 1873,
  "inputFingerprint": "9f2c…64 hex characters total…1ab7",
  "eligibleMoveCount": 24,
  "logLikes": [-71.2, -64.8, -59.1, -55.0, -52.3, -51.4, -52.9, -55.8, -60.2, -65.7, -72.4],
  "status": "scored"
}

Structural validation (decodeTargetEvidenceEnvelope, applied before any context check) requires all of:

  • schemaVersion == 1 and contractID == targetEvidenceContractID
  • moveScope == "account-owner-only"
  • playerColor is "white" or "black"
  • ownerUsername non-empty
  • source is already canonical (normalizedEvidenceSource(source) == source)
  • opponentElo finite and > 0
  • inputFingerprint.count == 64
  • every value in logLikes finite

then a status-dependent shape check, then a conditioning cross-check:

status Requires "scored" (or absent) eligibleMoveCount > 0 and logLikes.count == 11 "no-qualifying-owner-moves" eligibleMoveCount == 0 and logLikes empty opponentConditioning Requires "exact-lichess-opponent" source == "lichess" "neutral-lichess-1500" opponentElo == 1500

A missing status is treated as .scored, because the first generation of scored envelopes predates the field and must stay current. The "no-qualifying-owner-moves" receipt — written by encodeNoQualifyingOwnerMoves(context:) — is a terminal answer, not a failure: the game is valid, the no-Maia estimator serves it, and the scheduler stops retrying an inference that cannot succeed after every cooldown and app launch.

Legacy bare arrays are rejected here

encodeVector(_:) / decodeVector(_:) still read and write the old unversioned [Double] form for the retired maiaLogLikesJSON field, and decodeVector only accepts arrays of exactly 11 values. The target-evidence path never accepts a bare array. Those old vectors were scored over both players' moves, so a restored pre-fix backup must requeue rather than masquerade as corrected evidence.

docs.title: Staleness and merging
docs.text:
Evidence decodes only when the envelope matches the current scoring context on all six binding fields:

envelopeMatches  ==  playerColor          == context.playerColor
                  && ownerUsername        == context.ownerUsername
                  && source               == context.source
                  && opponentConditioning == context.opponentConditioning
                  && opponentElo          == context.opponentElo
                  && inputFingerprint     == context.inputFingerprint

A collection rename, a provider change, the owner switching sides, an edited opponent-rating tag, or any change to the move list therefore invalidates the payload and requeues the game.

Call Accepts decodeTargetEvidence(_:expectedContext:) context-matching envelopes with status == .scored → TargetEvidence hasResolvedTargetEvidence(_:expectedContext:) context-matching envelopes with either status → Bool isCurrentTargetEvidencePayload(_:) structurally valid envelopes, no context available preferredTargetEvidence(live:incoming:) live if valid, else incoming if valid, else nil

preferredTargetEvidence is the merge rule for backup restore (LibraryBackup.swift:201) and duplicate reconciliation (LibraryGameReconciliation.swift:533), where the destination collection's context is not yet known. Live authority wins whenever both sides are structurally valid, because the scheduler later applies the stronger context check and recomputes if the live payload turns out to be stale.

// Reading it back on the stats path.
guard let context = MaiaBackfillPolicy.scoringContext(
    white: game.white, black: game.black,
    username: candidate.username, source: candidate.source,
    moveText: game.moveText, tagsJSON: game.tagsJSON,
    whiteElo: whiteElo, blackElo: blackElo
) else { return nil }

let evidence = MaiaBackfillPolicy.decodeTargetEvidence(
    game.maiaTargetEvidenceV1JSON,
    expectedContext: context
)

let performance = EloEstimator.estimate(
    evalsJSON: game.annotationEvalsJSON,
    startIsWhite: true,
    color: context.playerColor,
    tc: .blitz,
    maiaEvidence: evidence,        // nil → the no-Maia v4.1 fallback
    termination: tags["Termination"]
)

That is exactly what StatsKernel does per game before building the Elo history. TargetEvidence carries logLikes, eligibleMoveCount, and opponentConditioning; the shipped coefficients consume the sums, not per-move means, so eligibleMoveCount is diagnostic metadata rather than a divisor. The conditioning case selects the reported serving path — .exactLichess → exactOpponentMaiaEnsemble, .neutralLichessPrior → neutral1500EvidenceExactArtifact.

docs.title: MaiaRankStyle
docs.text:
A one-function namespace mapping a Maia MultiPV rank onto a display tier, evaluated in this order:

rank < 0    → .poor       (played move was outside Maia's top-K)
rank == 0   → .best
rank <= 2   → .good
rank <= 4   → .moderate
otherwise   → .poor
Tier Rank band App-side color (not in the kit) .best 0 Color.green.opacity(0.25) .good 1–2 Color.yellow.opacity(0.25) .moderate 3–4 Color.orange.opacity(0.25) .poor ≥ 5, or −1 Color.red.opacity(0.2) 
// `playerMoveRank` is the played move's 0-based position in Maia's top-K,
// or −1 when it did not appear at all.
switch MaiaRankStyle.tier(forRank: playerMoveRank) {
case .best:     return Color.green.opacity(0.25)
case .good:     return Color.yellow.opacity(0.25)
case .moderate: return Color.orange.opacity(0.25)
case .poor:     return Color.red.opacity(0.2)
}

The kit stops at the tier. Color is forbidden in FianchettoKit, so each app owns its own mapping — which is also what lets iOS and Android use their native palettes while agreeing exactly on the bands. The two platforms' previously duplicated private helpers agreed exactly when they were folded into this type.

docs.title: Headless usage
docs.text:
fianchetto-cli maia runs the full grid sweep over JSON lines on stdin and emits maia_log_likes, positions_scored, opponent_conditioning, and opponent_elo per game — the same policy calls shown above, with a CoreML transport. It needs the model package.

Most of this page does not. The encoder, the policy index, both qualification walks, logSoftmaxAt over any logit array you supply, and the whole envelope codec are pure functions with no model dependency, so they can be exercised from a test, a script, or a scratch executable that never loads a network.

Not implemented today

The kit surface would support thin maia-encode, maia-qualify, maia-evidence, maia-moves, and maia-decode subcommands — token dumps, qualifying-ply listings, envelope encode/decode/validate, and policy-index lookups — none of which need the model. They are not in commandRegistry yet; see Tools/fianchetto-cli/SUBCOMMANDS.md for what ships.

docs.title: Cross-references
docs.text:
• EloEstimator.estimate(...) takes maiaEvidence: as a MaiaBackfillPolicy.TargetEvidence? and reports which serving path it used.
  • StatsKernel resolves the scoring context and decodes evidence per game while projecting the Elo history — available from the command line: fianchetto-cli project.
  • The v4.1 ensemble calibration model in EloCalibrationData consumes the vector as four of its 16 features: maia_mean_elo, maia_std_elo, and maia_argmax_elo (all under softmax(logLikes) over eloGrid), plus maia_ll_spread (max(logLikes) − min(logLikes)). The other twelve are the v3 move-quality features.
  • EloKernel.bestElo(from:) is the simpler live-analysis counterpart: argmax over a [Float: Double] rating → average-log-likelihood map.
  • Strength, Elo & accuracy for the estimator this evidence feeds, its time-control routing, and the stats pipeline that decodes it.
  • Analysis math for the accuracy features that ride alongside the Maia terms; Stores & the storage seam for where derived stats land.

docs.title: Network Clients
docs.text: Three REST clients: a Lichess tablebase probe, the Lichess opening explorer, and Chess.com / Lichess game import. All identify as User-Agent: "Fianchetto-ChessApp/1.0" and surface failures as ChessAPIError.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
public enum ChessAPIError: LocalizedError {
    case invalidUsername     // 404
    case networkError(String)
    case noGamesFound
    case rateLimited         // 429
    case unauthorized        // 401
}

ChessAPIError is LocalizedError with user-facing errorDescriptions (e.g. unauthorized → "Authentication required — add your Lichess API token…").

docs.title: TablebaseService — Syzygy probe
docs.text:
A cached actor over the Lichess tablebase endpoint (https://tablebase.lichess.ovh/standard). Results are cached by FEN.

public actor TablebaseService {
    public static let shared: TablebaseService
    public init()
    public static func pieceCount(for position: Position) -> Int
    public func probe(fen: String) async throws -> TablebaseResult
    public func clearCache()
}

import ChessCore
import FianchettoKit

if TablebaseService.pieceCount(for: position) <= 7 {   // tablebase is <= 7 pieces
    let result = try await TablebaseService.shared.probe(fen: position.consistentFEN)
    print(result.category)            // .win / .loss / .draw / .cursedWin / ...
    print(result.dtm ?? -1, result.dtz ?? -1)
    print(result.bestMove ?? "—")

    for move in result.moves {
        switch move.userVerdict {
        case .keepsWin: print("\(move.uci) keeps the win")
        case .draws:    print("\(move.uci) only draws")
        case .losesWin: print("\(move.uci) throws the win")
        case .unknown:  break
        }
    }
}

Use userVerdict, not category

Lichess reports each move's category from the opponent's perspective — the side to move after your move. So a move whose category is loss means the opponent is losing after your move, i.e. your move keeps the win. TablebaseMove.userVerdict is the single source of truth for the from-your-POV mapping; route every consumer through it instead of mapping categories inline.

public struct TablebaseResult: Sendable {
    public let category: Category    // win, loss, draw, cursedWin, blessedLoss, unknown
    public let dtm: Int?             // depth to mate
    public let dtz: Int?             // depth to zeroing
    public let bestMove: String?
    public let moves: [TablebaseMove]
}

public struct TablebaseMove: Sendable, Identifiable {
    public let uci: String
    public let san: String?
    public let category: TablebaseResult.Category
    public let dtm: Int?
    public let dtz: Int?
    public var userVerdict: UserVerdict   // .keepsWin | .draws | .losesWin | .unknown
}

docs.title: LichessExplorer — opening explorer
docs.text:
A cached actor over the Lichess opening explorer. Pick the database and (for the Lichess database) the rating bands.

public actor LichessExplorer {
    public static let shared: LichessExplorer
    public init()
    public func explore(fen: String,
                        database: ExplorerDatabase = .lichess,
                        ratings: [Int] = [1600, 1800, 2000, 2200, 2500],
                        token: String? = nil) async throws -> ExplorerResult
    public func clearCache()
}

public enum ExplorerDatabase: String, CaseIterable, Identifiable {
    case lichess = "Lichess"   // https://explorer.lichess.org/lichess
    case masters = "Masters"   // https://explorer.lichess.org/masters
}

let result = try await LichessExplorer.shared.explore(
    fen: position.fen,
    database: .lichess,
    ratings: [1600, 1800, 2000, 2200, 2500],
    token: nil                 // optional Lichess API token (Bearer)
)

print(result.totalGames, result.white, result.draws, result.black)
for move in result.moves.prefix(5) {
    print(move.san, move.totalGames, move.averageRating ?? 0)
}

Results are cached per "<database>:<fen>" (non-empty only). A 401 surfaces as .unauthorized (supply a token); a 429 as .rateLimited.

docs.title: ChessAPIService — game import
docs.text:
A fully nonisolated, Sendable class whose fetch+parse pipeline runs off the main actor. Its fetch methods are @concurrent — they run on the cooperative pool, not the caller's actor — and the optional progress callback hops to the main actor so @State writes stay correct.

public final class ChessAPIService: Sendable {
    public init()

    @concurrent public func fetchChessComGames(
        username: String,
        since: Date? = nil,
        onProgress: (@MainActor @Sendable (Int, Int) -> Void)? = nil
    ) async throws -> ChessComFetchResult

    @concurrent public func fetchLichessGames(
        username: String,
        since: Date? = nil,
        token: String? = nil
    ) async throws -> [PGNGame]

    @concurrent public func fetchLichessHistoryPages(
        username: String,
        since: Date? = nil,
        token: String? = nil,
        filters: ImportFilters? = nil,
        pageSize: Int = 1_000,
        resumingFrom cursor: LichessHistoryPageCursor? = nil,
        onPage: @Sendable (LichessHistoryPage) async throws -> Void
    ) async throws -> LichessHistoryCompletion
}

let service = ChessAPIService()

// Chess.com — walks the monthly archives; per-archive failures are collected
// rather than aborting the whole import.
let chesscom = try await service.fetchChessComGames(
    username: "MagnusCarlsen",
    since: Calendar.current.date(byAdding: .month, value: -6, to: .now)
) { done, total in
    print("archive \(done)/\(total)")   // @MainActor — safe to drive UI state
}
print(chesscom.games.count, "games")
if chesscom.isPartial { print("missed: \(chesscom.failedArchives)") }

// Lichess complete history — persist games and then the supplied cursor before
// returning from each callback. The next request cannot overtake that boundary.
let completion = try await service.fetchLichessHistoryPages(
    username: "DrNykterstein",
    token: lichessToken,
    pageSize: 5_000,
    resumingFrom: savedCursor
) { page in
    try await persistGamesAndThenCursor(
        page.games,
        cursor: page.resumeCursor
    )
}
print(completion.acknowledgedGameCount, "acknowledged games")

The Chess.com result and each Lichess page contain ChessCore PGNGame values (parsed via PGNParser.parse), so you can feed them straight into PreparedGameData for storage.

Lichess does not require a token for large histories. Authentication changes throughput: the documented export rates are 20 games/second anonymously, 30 games/second for an authenticated request, and 60 games/second when a token owner imports their own account. The bounded producer walks a fixed newest-first snapshot with one request in flight, and its Codable cursor makes the page callback a crash-recovery boundary. Retain that cursor and wait at least a minute after a 429 rather than restarting the history.

docs.title: Error handling pattern
docs.text:
do {
    _ = try await service.fetchLichessGames(username: name, token: token)
} catch ChessAPIError.unauthorized {
    // prompt for an API token
} catch ChessAPIError.invalidUsername {
    // 404 — no such user
} catch ChessAPIError.rateLimited {
    // 429 — back off
} catch ChessAPIError.noGamesFound {
    // empty result
} catch {
    // ChessAPIError.networkError(message) or a transport error
}

docs.title: Network Clients & Game Import
docs.text:
The three REST clients FianchettoKit owns — Chess.com / Lichess game import, the Lichess opening explorer, and the Lichess Syzygy tablebase — over one shared URLSession shim. Most of the code here is not transport: it is the decision rules that stop an interrupted import from losing games and an incremental re-fetch from advancing a cursor past archives it never read.

Networking follows Fianchetto's higher deployment floor (iOS 18 / macOS 15) while ChessCore keeps a generous community floor (iOS 13 / macOS 10.15), so the clients live here, on top of ChessCore's PGNGame / PGNParser / Position.

File What it holds ChessAPIService.swift Chess.com sweep, Lichess export + resumable history walk, ImportFilters, ChessAPIError, GameUpdatePlanner LichessGameStreamDecoder.swift NDJSON framer, both pagination accumulators, LichessGamePaginationError LichessHistoryImportCheckpoint.swift LichessHistoryImportIdentity, LichessHistoryImportCheckpoint LichessExplorer.swift explorer actor, ExplorerResult / ExplorerMove / ExplorerDatabase TablebaseService.swift Syzygy actor, TablebaseResult / TablebaseMove URLSession+DataResult.swift the cancellation-correct dataResult shim

ChessPlatform (.chesscom = "Chess.com", .lichess = "Lichess") is the display vocabulary. It is not what GameUpdatePlanner.fetch reads: that compares a collection's stored source against the lowercase literal "lichess" and treats everything else as Chess.com.

docs.title: Concurrency and isolation
docs.text:
public nonisolated final class ChessAPIService: Sendable { … }
public nonisolated enum ChessAPIError: LocalizedError { … }
public nonisolated enum GameUpdatePlanner { … }

The fetch methods are @concurrent, not merely nonisolated: under the project's NonisolatedNonsendingByDefault setting a plain nonisolated async method runs on the caller's actor, so a sweep started from a MainActor view would parse every month's PGN on the main thread. The class is Sendable (final, holding only two immutable URLSessions) so a view can hold one and hand it to off-main work, and ChessAPIError is nonisolated because its cases and LocalizedError witness are thrown from those pool-resident methods. Progress callbacks are typed (@MainActor @Sendable (Int, Int) -> Void)? and fire once per progress tick — one archive month — so @State writes stay correct without flooding main.

docs.title: Transport: URLSession.dataResult
docs.text:
dataResult(for:) / dataResult(from:) back-deploy URLSession.data(for:) to iOS 13 / macOS 10.15 and are used by all three clients. They exist because the async data(for:) / bytes(for:) are iOS 15 / macOS 12 only and swift-corelibs-foundation has no async bytes(for:) at all — only the completion-handler dataTask is available everywhere.

Cancellation can race all three phases: before the task exists, after it starts, after its completion handler fires. One NSLock-guarded box holds the task and the continuation and gives the continuation exactly one terminal path.

dataResult(for:) =
  withTaskCancellationHandler {
      try Task.checkCancellation()
      withCheckedThrowingContinuation { c in
          let task = dataTask(with: request) { d, r, e in state.complete(data: d, response: r, error: e) }
          state.start(task: task, continuation: c)
      }
  } onCancel: { state.cancel() }

start(task:continuation:)
  isCancelled already -> isCompleted = true; task.cancel(); resume(throwing: CancellationError())
                         // cancel()-before-resume() is NOT guaranteed to fire every
                         // Foundation implementation's completion handler
  otherwise           -> store task + continuation; task.resume()

cancel()
  isCancelled = true
  isCompleted || continuation == nil -> no-op
  otherwise -> isCompleted = true; nil both fields; task.cancel(); resume(throwing: CancellationError())

complete(data:response:error:)
  isCompleted        -> no-op                       // the ignored late callback
  error != nil       -> resume(throwing: error)
  data && response   -> resume(returning: (data, response))
  otherwise          -> resume(throwing: URLError(.badServerResponse))

docs.title: Session budgets
docs.text:
Every request sends User-Agent: Fianchetto-ChessApp/1.0.

Session Request Resource Sized for ChessAPIService.session 30 s 180 s one Chess.com archive month per request ChessAPIService.streamSession 60 s 7_200 s one long Lichess account export; the 60 s idle covers server-side pauses between games LichessExplorer.session 10 s — one position lookup TablebaseService.session 10 s — one FEN probe

Without timeoutIntervalForResource, URLSession enforces only the per-segment idle timer and a perfectly slow stream stays open forever — but 180 s, right for month-shaped archives, guarantees failure for a whole-account export. Hence two sessions.

docs.title: Import filters
docs.text:
ImportTimeControl raw values (bullet, blitz, rapid, classical) match Lichess perfType exactly so they can be sent verbatim; chessComTimeClass maps .classical to "standard", which is what Chess.com writes in its TimeClass PGN tag. ImportColor.any means "no restriction" everywhere. All ImportFilters fields default to nil, so existing callers are unaffected.

isActive = ratedOnly != nil
        || timeControls?.isEmpty == false
        || (color != nil && color != .any)
        || since != nil
Filter Lichess (server-side) Chess.com (client-side) ratedOnly rated=true / rated=false !game.event.contains("(Unrated)") timeControls perfType= raw values .sorted().joined(separator: ",") TimeClass tag vs chessComTimeClass color color=white / color=black, omitted for .any lowercased username vs White / Black since since= ms, merged with the incremental cursor Date tag parsed as "YYYY.MM.DD", keep gameDate >= since

Chess.com has no server-side filter API; the client-side predicate runs only when filters.isActive, so an inactive bundle costs nothing.

docs.title: Chess.com: the archive sweep
docs.text:
Archives are partitioned by UTC calendar month, and the month filter never uses Calendar.current:

chessComArchiveURLs(archives, notBefore: since)
  since == nil -> keep everything
  calendar = Calendar(identifier: .gregorian), timeZone = GMT+0
  (sinceYear, sinceMonth) = components of `since`
  per URL: split on "/", read the last two path components as year, month
      fewer than 2 components, or non-integer year/month  -> KEEP (return true)
      keep when  year > sinceYear || (year == sinceYear && month >= sinceMonth)

A device-local calendar would let a positive-UTC-offset device already be in the next local month shortly before a transition and skip the still-current UTC archive permanently. Malformed entries are kept on purpose, so the validated fetch loop reports them as a partial failure instead of treating an incomplete archive list as a clean sweep.

The sweep then walks filtered.reversed() — newest month first — reporting (index + 1, total) once per month.

Stage Condition Outcome archives index 404 / 429 / other non-2xx invalidUsername / rateLimited / networkError("HTTP <code>") archives index no top-level archives array of strings noGamesFound per archive scheme != https or host != api.chess.com added to failedArchives, never fetched per archive 429 rateLimited — aborts the whole sweep per archive non-2xx, non-HTTPURLResponse, empty or non-UTF-8 body added to failedArchives per archive CancellationError rethrown immediately — control flow, not a failed month per archive a typed ChessAPIError rethrown verbatim, so an auth problem is not coerced into a rate-limit toast per archive anything else added to failedArchives, sweep continues

Each server-supplied archive URL is re-validated before "/pgn" is appended, so a compromised index cannot redirect fetches elsewhere. PGNParser is deliberately permissive for hand-authored imports, so archives get a stricter boundary before they count as a successful month:

isStructurallyValidChessComArchive(games)
  games non-empty, and EVERY game has
      White  trimmed and non-empty
      Black  trimmed and non-empty
      Result trimmed and in ["1-0", "0-1", "1/2-1/2", "*"]

Move-less and aborted games stay valid; what this rejects is an HTML error page or truncated body being parsed into a zero-or-garbage-game month.

Finally guard !finalGames.isEmpty || !failedArchives.isEmpty else { throw .noGamesFound }: a sweep where every listed archive failed is partial, not "no games". That distinction is what stops GameUpdatePlanner — which normalizes noGamesFound into a clean empty result whenever a watermark is present — from advancing the watermark past months it never read.

import ChessCore
import FianchettoKit

let api = ChessAPIService()

let sweep = try await api.fetchChessComGames(
    username: "MagnusCarlsen",
    since: lastSyncDate,
    filters: ImportFilters(
        ratedOnly: true,
        timeControls: [.blitz, .rapid],
        color: .white
    )
) { completed, total in
    // @MainActor — one tick per archive month, safe to write @State directly.
    importProgress = Double(completed) / Double(total)
}

if sweep.isPartial {
    // Do NOT stamp lastSyncDate, or these months are skipped forever.
    print("failed archives:", sweep.failedArchives)
}

sweep.games are ordinary ChessCore PGNGame values, so they feed the analysis path directly. Available from the command line: fianchetto-cli annotate (per-ply evals) and fianchetto-cli estimate (rating estimate from them).

docs.title: Lichess: one base request, three shapes
docs.text:
lichessBaseRequest(username:since:filters:) is the single source of account normalization and every filter; the one-shot snapshot and the resumable page producer both start there, so their query shapes cannot drift.
